<h1 id="box-platform-api-events">Events</h1>

Events provide a way for an
application to subscribe to
any actions performed by
any user, users, or service in an enterprise.

## List user and enterprise events

<a id="opIdget_events"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /events`

Returns up to a year of past events for a given user
or for the entire enterprise.

By default this returns events for the authenticated user. To retrieve events
for the entire enterprise, set the `stream_type` to `admin_logs_streaming`
for live monitoring of new events, or `admin_logs` for querying across
historical events. The user making the API call will
need to have admin privileges, and the application will need to have the
scope `manage enterprise properties` checked.

<h3 id="list-user-and-enterprise-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stream_type|query|string|false|Defines the type of events that are returned<br><br>* `all` returns everything for a user and is the default<br>* `changes` returns events that may cause file tree changes<br>  such as file updates or collaborations.<br>* `sync` is similar to `changes` but only applies to synced folders<br>* `admin_logs` returns all events for an entire enterprise and<br>  requires the user making the API call to have admin permissions. This<br>  stream type is for programmatically pulling from a 1 year history of<br>  events across all users within the enterprise and within a<br>  `created_after` and `created_before` time frame. The complete history<br>  of events will be returned in chronological order based on the event<br>  time, but latency will be much higher than `admin_logs_streaming`.<br>* `admin_logs_streaming` returns all events for an entire enterprise and<br>  requires the user making the API call to have admin permissions. This<br>  stream type is for polling for recent events across all users within<br>  the enterprise. Latency will be much lower than `admin_logs`, but<br>  events will not be returned in chronological order and may<br>  contain duplicates.|
|stream_position|query|string|false|The location in the event stream to start receiving events from.<br><br>* `now` will return an empty list events and<br>the latest stream position for initialization.<br>* `0` or `null` will return all events.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Limits the number of events returned.<br><br>Note: Sometimes, the events less than the limit requested can be returned<br>even when there may be more events remaining. This is primarily done in<br>the case where a number of events have already been retrieved and these<br>retrieved events are returned rather than delaying for an unknown amount<br>of time to see if there are any more results.|
|event_type|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of events to filter by. This can only be used when<br>requesting the events with a `stream_type` of `admin_logs` or<br>`adming_logs_streaming`. For any other `stream_type` this value will be<br>ignored.|
|created_after|query|string(date-time)|false|The lower bound date and time to return events for. This can only be used<br>when requesting the events with a `stream_type` of `admin_logs`. For any<br>other `stream_type` this value will be ignored.|
|created_before|query|string(date-time)|false|The upper bound date and time to return events for. This can only be used<br>when requesting the events with a `stream_type` of `admin_logs`. For any<br>other `stream_type` this value will be ignored.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|stream_type|all|
|stream_type|changes|
|stream_type|sync|
|stream_type|admin_logs|
|stream_type|admin_logs_streaming|

## Get events long poll endpoint

<a id="opIdoptions_events"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/events \
  -X OPTIONS \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`OPTIONS /events`

Returns a list of real-time servers that can be used for long-polling updates
to the [event stream](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-events).

Long polling is the concept where a HTTP request is kept open until the
server sends a response, then repeating the process over and over to receive
updated responses.

Long polling the event stream can only be used for user events, not for
enterprise events.

To use long polling, first use this endpoint to retrieve a list of long poll
URLs. Next, make a long poll request to any of the provided URLs.

When an event occurs in monitored account a response with the value
`new_change` will be sent. The response contains no other details as
it only serves as a prompt to take further action such as sending a
request to the [events endpoint](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-events) with the last known
`stream_position`.

After the server sends this response it closes the connection. You must now
repeat the long poll process to begin listening for events again.

If no events occur for a while and the connection times out you will
receive a response with the value `reconnect`. When you receive this response
you’ll make another call to this endpoint to restart the process.

If you receive no events in `retry_timeout` seconds then you will need to
make another request to the real-time server (one of the URLs in the response
for this endpoint). This might be necessary due to network errors.

Finally, if you receive a `max_retries` error when making a request to the
real-time server, you should start over by making a call to this endpoint
first.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "chunk_size": 1,
  "entries": [
    {
      "type": "realtime_server",
      "url": "http://2.realtime.services.box.net/subscribe?channel=cc807c9c4869ffb1c81a&stream_type=all",
      "ttl": "10",
      "max_retries": "10",
      "retry_timeout": 610
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong"
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456"
}
```

<h1 id="box-platform-api-file-requests">File requests</h1>

File Requests provide a fast and
secure way to request files and associated metadata
from anyone.
Users can create new file requests
based on an existing file request,
update file request settings, activate, deactivate, and delete
file requests programmatically.

## Get file request

<a id="opIdget_file_requests_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/file_requests/123 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /file_requests/{file_request_id}`

Retrieves the information about a file request.

<h3 id="get-file-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_request_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a file request.<br><br>The ID for any file request can be determined<br>by visiting a file request builder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/filerequest/123`<br>the `file_request_id` is `123`.|

## Update file request

<a id="opIdput_file_requests_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/file_requests/123 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Please upload required documents",
    "description": "Please upload required documents",
    "status": "active",
    "is_email_required": true,
    "is_description_required": true,
    "expires_at": "2020-09-28T10:53:43-08:00"
  }'
```

`PUT /file_requests/{file_request_id}`

Updates a file request. This can be used to activate or
deactivate a file request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Please upload required documents",
  "description": "Please upload required documents",
  "status": "active",
  "is_email_required": true,
  "is_description_required": true,
  "expires_at": "2020-09-28T10:53:43-08:00"
}
```

<h3 id="update-file-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_request_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a file request.<br><br>The ID for any file request can be determined<br>by visiting a file request builder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/filerequest/123`<br>the `file_request_id` is `123`.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|
|body|body|[FileRequestUpdateRequest](#schemafilerequestupdaterequest)|false|none|
|» title|body|string|false|An optional new title for the file request. This can be<br>used to change the title of the file request.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional new description for the file request. This can be<br>used to change the description of the file request.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» status|body|string|false|An optional new status of the file request.<br><br>When the status is set to `inactive`, the file request<br>will no longer accept new submissions, and any visitor<br>to the file request URL will receive a `HTTP 404` status<br>code.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» is_email_required|body|boolean|false|Whether a file request submitter is required to provide<br>their email address.<br><br>When this setting is set to true, the Box UI will show<br>an email field on the file request form.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» is_description_required|body|boolean|false|Whether a file request submitter is required to provide<br>a description of the files they are submitting.<br><br>When this setting is set to true, the Box UI will show<br>a description field on the file request form.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The date after which a file request will no longer accept new<br>submissions.<br><br>After this date, the `status` will automatically be set to<br>`inactive`.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|active|
|» status|inactive|

<h3 id="update-file-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the updated file request object.|[FileRequest](#schemafilerequest)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned when the access token provided in the `Authorization` header<br>is not recognized or not provided.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have all the permissions to complete the<br>update.<br><br>* `access_denied_insufficient_permissions` when the authenticated user<br>does not have access to update the file request.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the file request is not found, or the user does not<br>have access to the associated folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Returned if the `file_request_id` is not in a recognized format.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|412|Precondition Failed|Returns an error when the `If-Match` header does not match<br>the current `etag` value of the file request. This indicates that the<br>file request has changed since it was last requested.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returns an empty response when the file request has been successfully<br>deleted.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned when the access token provided in the `Authorization` header<br>is not recognized or not provided.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the file request is not found or has already been deleted,<br>or the user does not have access to the associated folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Returned if the `file_request_id` is not in a recognized format.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Copy file request

<a id="opIdpost_file_requests_id_copy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/file_requests/123/copy \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Please upload required documents",
    "description": "Please upload required documents",
    "status": "active",
    "is_email_required": true,
    "is_description_required": true,
    "expires_at": "2020-09-28T10:53:43-08:00",
    "folder": {
      "type": "folder",
      "id": "42037322"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /file_requests/{file_request_id}/copy`

Copies an existing file request that is already present on one folder,
and applies it to another folder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Please upload required documents",
  "description": "Please upload required documents",
  "status": "active",
  "is_email_required": true,
  "is_description_required": true,
  "expires_at": "2020-09-28T10:53:43-08:00",
  "folder": {
    "type": "folder",
    "id": "42037322"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="copy-file-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_request_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a file request.<br><br>The ID for any file request can be determined<br>by visiting a file request builder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/filerequest/123`<br>the `file_request_id` is `123`.|
|body|body|[FileRequestCopyRequest](#schemafilerequestcopyrequest)|false|none|
|» title|body|string|false|An optional new title for the file request. This can be<br>used to change the title of the file request.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional new description for the file request. This can be<br>used to change the description of the file request.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» status|body|string|false|An optional new status of the file request.<br><br>When the status is set to `inactive`, the file request<br>will no longer accept new submissions, and any visitor<br>to the file request URL will receive a `HTTP 404` status<br>code.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» is_email_required|body|boolean|false|Whether a file request submitter is required to provide<br>their email address.<br><br>When this setting is set to true, the Box UI will show<br>an email field on the file request form.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» is_description_required|body|boolean|false|Whether a file request submitter is required to provide<br>a description of the files they are submitting.<br><br>When this setting is set to true, the Box UI will show<br>a description field on the file request form.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The date after which a file request will no longer accept new<br>submissions.<br><br>After this date, the `status` will automatically be set to<br>`inactive`.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» folder|body|object|true|The folder to associate the new file request to.|
|» » type|body|string|false|The value will always be `folder`.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the folder to associate the new<br>file request to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|active|
|» status|inactive|
|» » type|folder|

> 200 Response

<h1 id="box-platform-api-file-version-legal-holds">File version legal holds</h1>

A legal hold is a process that an enterprise
can use to preserve all forms of potentially relevant
information when
litigation is pending or reasonably anticipated.
A File Version Legal Hold represents all the policies that
are assigned to a specific file version.

## Get file version legal hold

<a id="opIdget_file_version_legal_holds_id"></a>

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

## List file version legal holds

<a id="opIdget_file_version_legal_holds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/file_version_legal_holds?policy_id=133870' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /file_version_legal_holds`

Get a list of file versions on legal hold for a legal hold
assignment.

Due to ongoing re-architecture efforts this API might not return all file
versions for this policy ID.

Instead, this API will only return file versions held in the legacy
architecture. Two new endpoints will available to request any file versions
held in the new architecture.

For file versions held in the new architecture, the `GET
/legal_hold_policy_assignments/:id/file_versions_on_hold` API can be used to
return all past file versions available for this policy assignment, and the
`GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments/:id/files_on_hold` API can be used to
return any current (latest) versions of a file under legal hold.

The `GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments?policy_id={id}` API can be used to
find a list of policy assignments for a given policy ID.

Once the re-architecture is completed this API will be deprecated.

<h3 id="list-file-version-legal-holds-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|policy_id|query|string|true|The ID of the legal hold policy to get the file version legal<br>holds for.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-file-version-retentions">File version retentions</h1>

A retention policy blocks permanent
deletion of content for a specified amount of time.
A file version retention is a record for a retained file.

## List file version retentions

<a id="opIdget_file_version_retentions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/file_version_retentions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /file_version_retentions`

Retrieves all file version retentions for the given enterprise.

**Note**:
File retention API is now **deprecated**.
To get information about files and file versions under retention,
see [files under retention](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-retention-policy-assignments-id-files-under-retention) or [file versions under retention](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-retention-policy-assignments-id-file-versions-under-retention) endpoints.

<h3 id="list-file-version-retentions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|query|string|false|Filters results by files with this ID.|
|file_version_id|query|string|false|Filters results by file versions with this ID.|
|policy_id|query|string|false|Filters results by the retention policy with this ID.|
|disposition_action|query|string|false|Filters results by the retention policy with this disposition<br>action.|
|disposition_before|query|string|false|Filters results by files that will have their disposition<br>come into effect before this date.|
|disposition_after|query|string|false|Filters results by files that will have their disposition<br>come into effect after this date.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|disposition_action|permanently_delete|
|disposition_action|remove_retention|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-file-versions">File versions</h1>

A set of endpoints used to manage specific
versions of a file.

## List all file versions

<a id="opIdget_files_id_versions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345/versions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /files/{file_id}/versions`

Retrieve a list of the past versions for a file.

Versions are only tracked by Box users with premium accounts. To fetch the ID
of the current version of a file, use the `GET /file/:id` API.

<h3 id="list-all-file-versions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|

`DELETE /files/{file_id}/versions/{file_version_id}`

Move a file version to the trash.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|file_version_id|path|string|true|The ID of the file version.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|

## Promote file version

<a id="opIdpost_files_id_versions_current"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345/versions/current \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "file_version"
  }'
```

`POST /files/{file_id}/versions/current`

Promote a specific version of a file.

If previous versions exist, this method can be used to
promote one of the older versions to the top of the version history.

This creates a new copy of the old version and puts it at the
top of the versions history. The file will have the exact same contents
as the older version, with the same hash digest, `etag`, and
name as the original.

Other properties such as comments do not get updated to their
former values.

Don't use this endpoint to restore Box Notes,
as it works with file formats such as PDF, DOC,
PPTX or similar.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "11446498",
  "type": "file_version"
}
```

<h3 id="promote-file-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» id|body|string|false|The file version ID.|
|» type|body|string|false|The type to promote.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|file_version|

> Example responses

<h1 id="box-platform-api-files">Files</h1>

Files, together with Folders,
are at the core of the Box API.
Files can be uploaded and downloaded,
as well as hold important metadata
information about the content.

## Get file information

<a id="opIdget_files_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /files/{file_id}`

Retrieves the details about a file.

<h3 id="get-file-information-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.<br><br>Additionally this field can be used to query any metadata<br>applied to the file by specifying the `metadata` field as well<br>as the scope and key of the template to retrieve, for example<br>`?fields=metadata.enterprise_12345.contractTemplate`.|
|if-none-match|header|string|false|Ensures an item is only returned if it has changed.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `304 Not Modified` if the item has not<br>changed since.|
|boxapi|header|string|false|The URL, and optional password, for the shared link of this item.<br><br>This header can be used to access items that have not been<br>explicitly shared with a user.<br><br>Use the format `shared_link=[link]` or if a password is required then<br>use `shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`.<br><br>This header can be used on the file or folder shared, as well as on any files<br>or folders nested within the item.|
|x-rep-hints|header|string \| null|false|A header required to request specific `representations`<br>of a file. Use this in combination with the `fields` query<br>parameter to request a specific file representation.<br><br>The general format for these representations is<br>`X-Rep-Hints: [...]` where `[...]` is one or many<br>hints in the format `[fileType?query]`.<br><br>For example, to request a `png` representation in `32x32`<br>as well as `64x64` pixel dimensions provide the following<br>hints.<br><br>`x-rep-hints: [jpg?dimensions=32x32][jpg?dimensions=64x64]`<br><br>Additionally, a `text` representation is available for all<br>document file types in Box using the `[extracted_text]`<br>representation.<br><br>`x-rep-hints: [extracted_text]`.|

<h3 id="get-file-information-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a file object.<br><br>Not all available fields are returned by default. Use the<br>[fields](#parameter-fields) query parameter to explicitly request<br>any specific fields.|[File--Full](#schemafile--full)|
|304|Not Modified|Returns an empty response when the `If-None-Match` header matches<br>the current `etag` value of the folder. This indicates that the folder<br>has not changed since it was last requested.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned when the access token provided in the `Authorization` header<br>is not recognized or not provided.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the file is not found, or the user does not<br>have access to the file.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Returned if the `file_id` is not in a recognized format.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Returns an error if an action is performed on a file with an<br>incorrect media type.<br><br>* `unsupported_media_type` when requesting an `expiring_embed_link`<br>  for a file that is not supported by Box Embed.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Update file

<a id="opIdput_files_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "NewFile.txt",
    "description": "The latest reports. Automatically updated",
    "parent": {
      "id": "123",
      "user_id": "12346930"
    },
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "permissions": {
        "can_download": true
      },
      "one_time_passcode": {
        "mode": "none"
      }
    },
    "lock": {
      "access": "lock",
      "expires_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "is_download_prevented": true
    },
    "disposition_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": "open"
    },
    "collections": [
      {
        "id": "11446498",
        "type": "file"
      }
    ],
    "tags": [
      "approved"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /files/{file_id}`

Updates a file. This can be used to rename or move a file,
create a shared link, or lock a file.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "NewFile.txt",
  "description": "The latest reports. Automatically updated",
  "parent": {
    "id": "123",
    "user_id": "12346930"
  },
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true
    },
    "one_time_passcode": {
      "mode": "none"
    }
  },
  "lock": {
    "access": "lock",
    "expires_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "is_download_prevented": true
  },
  "disposition_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "permissions": {
    "can_download": "open"
  },
  "collections": [
    {
      "id": "11446498",
      "type": "file"
    }
  ],
  "tags": [
    "approved"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|An optional different name for the file. This can be used to<br>rename the file.<br><br>File names must be unique within their parent folder. The name check is case-insensitive, so a file<br>named `New File` cannot be created in a parent folder that already contains a folder named `new file`.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description for a file. This can be seen in the right-hand sidebar panel<br>when viewing a file in the Box web app. Additionally, this index is used in<br>the search index of the file, allowing users to find the file by the content<br>in the description.|
|» parent|body|object|false|none|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of parent item.|
|» » user_id|body|string|false|The input for `user_id` is optional. Moving to non-root folder is not allowed when `user_id` is present. Parent folder id should be zero when `user_id` is provided.|
|» shared_link|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string \| null|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br>Passwords must now be at least eight characters<br>long and include a number, upper case letter, or<br>a non-numeric or non-alphabetic character.<br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared links.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » one_time_passcode|body|object|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableNone](#schemasharedlinkotpwritablenone)|false|One-time-passcode (OTP) enforcement is turned off. The shared link is<br>accessible without any one-time-passcode verification.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableOpen](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableopen)|false|Any anonymous recipient can request a one-time-passcode to any email<br>address and access the shared link after verifying it. Collaborators<br>and registered Box users access the link without being prompted.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableAllowlist](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableallowlist)|false|Anonymous recipients can request a one-time-passcode only when they<br>enter an email that matches an entry on the `allowlist`.|
|» lock|body|object \| null|false|Defines a lock on an item. This prevents the item from being<br>moved, renamed, or otherwise changed by anyone other than the user<br>who created the lock.<br><br>Set this to `null` to remove the lock.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The type of this object.|
|» » expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Defines the time at which the lock expires.|
|» » is_download_prevented|body|boolean|false|Defines if the file can be downloaded while it is locked.|
|» disposition_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The retention expiration timestamp for the given file. This<br>date cannot be shortened once set on a file.|
|» permissions|body|object|false|Defines who can download a file.|
|» » can_download|body|string|false|Defines who is allowed to download this file. The possible<br>values are either `open` for everyone or `company` for<br>the other members of the user's enterprise.<br><br>This setting overrides the download permissions that are<br>normally part of the `role` of a collaboration. When set to<br>`company`, this essentially removes the download option for<br>external users with `viewer` or `editor` a roles.|
|» collections|body|[object]|false|An array of collections to make this file<br>a member of. Currently<br>we only support the `favorites` collection.<br><br>To get the ID for a collection, use the<br>[List all collections][1] endpoint.<br><br>Passing an empty array `[]` or `null` will remove<br>the file from all collections.<br><br>[1]: https://developer.box.com/reference/get-collections|
|» » id|body|string|false|The unique identifier for this object.|
|» » type|body|string|false|The type for this object.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|The tags for this item. These tags are shown in<br>the Box web app and mobile apps next to an item.<br><br>To add or remove a tag, retrieve the item's current tags,<br>modify them, and then update this field.<br><br>There is a limit of 100 tags per item, and 10,000<br>unique tags per enterprise.|

|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|
|» » access|lock|
|» » can_download|open|
|» » can_download|company|

|200|OK|Returns a file object.<br><br>Not all available fields are returned by default. Use the<br>[fields](#parameter-fields) query parameter to explicitly request<br>any specific fields.|[File--Full](#schemafile--full)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned when the new retention time > maximum retention length.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned when the access token provided in the `Authorization` header<br>is not recognized or not provided.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have all the permissions to complete the<br>update.<br><br>* `access_denied_insufficient_permissions` returned<br>when the authenticated user does not have access<br>to the destination folder to move the file to.<br>* Returned when retention time is shorter or equal to current retention<br>timestamp.<br>* Returned when a `file_id` that is not under retention is entered.<br>* Returned when a file that is retained but the disposition action is set<br>to `remove_retention`<br>* `forbidden_by_policy` is returned if copying a folder is<br>forbidden due to information barrier restrictions.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the file is not found, or the user does not<br>have access to the file.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Returned if the `file_id` is not in a recognized format.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|412|Precondition Failed|Returns an error when the `If-Match` header does not match<br>the current `etag` value of the file. This indicates that the file<br>has changed since it was last requested.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Delete file

<a id="opIddelete_files_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /files/{file_id}`

Deletes a file, either permanently or by moving it to
the trash.

The enterprise settings determine whether the item will
be permanently deleted from Box or moved to the trash.

<h3 id="delete-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|

## Copy file

<a id="opIdpost_files_id_copy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345/copy \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "FileCopy.txt",
    "version": "0",
    "parent": {
      "id": "0"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /files/{file_id}/copy`

Creates a copy of a file.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "FileCopy.txt",
  "version": "0",
  "parent": {
    "id": "0"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="copy-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|An optional new name for the copied file.<br><br>There are some restrictions to the file name. Names containing<br>non-printable ASCII characters, forward and backward slashes<br>(`/`, `\`), and protected names like `.` and `..` are<br>automatically sanitized by removing the non-allowed<br>characters.|
|» version|body|string|false|An optional ID of the specific file version to copy.|
|» parent|body|object|true|The destination folder to copy the file to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of folder to copy the file to.|

## Get file thumbnail

<a id="opIdget_files_id_thumbnail_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345/thumbnail.png \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /files/{file_id}/thumbnail.{extension}`

Retrieves a thumbnail, or smaller image representation, of a file.

Sizes of `32x32`,`64x64`, `128x128`, and `256x256` can be returned in
the `.png` format and sizes of `32x32`, `160x160`, and `320x320`
can be returned in the `.jpg` format.

Thumbnails can be generated for the image and video file formats listed
[found on our community site][1].

[1]: https://community.box.com/t5/Migrating-and-Previewing-Content/File-Types-and-Fonts-Supported-in-Box-Content-Preview/ta-p/327

<h3 id="get-file-thumbnail-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|extension|path|string|true|The file format for the thumbnail.|
|min_height|query|integer|false|The minimum height of the thumbnail.|
|min_width|query|integer|false|The minimum width of the thumbnail.|
|max_height|query|integer|false|The maximum height of the thumbnail.|
|max_width|query|integer|false|The maximum width of the thumbnail.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|extension|png|
|extension|jpg|

<h3 id="get-file-thumbnail-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|When a thumbnail can be created the thumbnail data will be<br>returned in the body of the response.|Inline|
|202|Accepted|Sometimes generating a thumbnail can take a few seconds. In these<br>situations the API returns a `Location`-header pointing to a<br>placeholder graphic for this file type.<br><br>The placeholder graphic can be used in a user interface until the<br>thumbnail generation has completed. The `Retry-After`-header indicates<br>when to the thumbnail will be ready. At that time, retry this endpoint<br>to retrieve the thumbnail.|None|
|302|Found|Returns an error when Box is not able to create a thumbnail for this<br>file type.<br><br>Instead, a `Location`-header pointing to a placeholder graphic for<br>this file type will be returned.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if some of the parameters are missing or<br>not valid.<br><br>* `requested_preview_unavailable` - an incorrect dimension was<br>  requested. This will happen if the dimension requested is<br>  larger or smaller than the available file sizes for the thumbnail<br>  format, or when when any of the size constraints contradict<br>  each other.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned when the access token provided in the `Authorization` header<br>is not recognized or not provided.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the file is not found, or the user does not<br>have access to the file, or for additional reasons.<br><br>* `preview_cannot_be_generated` - Box does not support thumbnails<br>  for this type of file.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Retry-After|integer|int64|The time in seconds after which the thumbnail will be available.<br><br>Your application  only attempt to get the thumbnail again after<br>this time.|
|202|Location|string|url|A pointer to a placeholder graphic that can be used until the<br>thumbnail has been generated.|
|302|Location|string|url|A pointer to a placeholder graphic that can be used for this<br>file type.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

<h1 id="box-platform-api-folder-locks">Folder Locks</h1>

Folder locks define access restrictions
placed by folder owners to prevent
specific folders from being moved or deleted.

## List folder locks

<a id="opIdget_folder_locks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/folder_locks?folder_id=12345' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /folder_locks`

Retrieves folder lock details for a given folder.

You must be authenticated as the owner or co-owner of the folder to
use this endpoint.

<h3 id="list-folder-locks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|query|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|

## Create folder lock

<a id="opIdpost_folder_locks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/folder_locks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "locked_operations": {
      "move": true,
      "delete": true
    },
    "folder": {
      "type": "folder",
      "id": "1234567890"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /folder_locks`

Creates a folder lock on a folder, preventing it from being moved and/or
deleted.

You must be authenticated as the owner or co-owner of the folder to
use this endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "locked_operations": {
    "move": true,
    "delete": true
  },
  "folder": {
    "type": "folder",
    "id": "1234567890"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-folder-lock-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» locked_operations|body|object|false|The operations to lock for the folder. If `locked_operations` is<br>included in the request, both `move` and `delete` must also be<br>included and both set to `true`.|
|» » move|body|boolean|true|Whether moving the folder should be locked.|
|» » delete|body|boolean|true|Whether deleting the folder should be locked.|
|» folder|body|object|true|The folder to apply the lock to.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The content type the lock is being applied to. Only `folder`<br>is supported.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the folder.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "folder": {
    "id": "12345",
    "etag": "1",
    "type": "folder",
    "sequence_id": {},
    "name": "Contracts"
  },
  "id": "12345678",
  "type": "folder_lock",
  "created_by": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "user"
  },
  "created_at": "2020-09-14T23:12:53Z",
  "locked_operations": {
    "move": true,
    "delete": true
  },
  "lock_type": "freeze"
}
```

```json
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456"
}
```

An example might be an unknown option<br>for an `enum` or `multiSelect` field.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-folders">Folders</h1>

Folders, together with Files,
are at the core of the Box API.
Folders can be uploaded and downloaded,
as well as hold important metadata
information about the content.

## Get folder information

<a id="opIdget_folders_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/12345 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /folders/{folder_id}`

Retrieves details for a folder, including the first 100 entries
in the folder.

Passing `sort`, `direction`, `offset`, and `limit`
parameters in query allows you to manage the
list of returned
[folder items](https://developer.box.com/reference/resources/folder--full#param-item-collection).

To fetch more items within the folder, use the
[Get items in a folder](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-folders-id-items) endpoint.

<h3 id="get-folder-information-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.<br><br>Additionally this field can be used to query any metadata<br>applied to the file by specifying the `metadata` field as well<br>as the scope and key of the template to retrieve, for example<br>`?fields=metadata.enterprise_12345.contractTemplate`.|
|if-none-match|header|string|false|Ensures an item is only returned if it has changed.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `304 Not Modified` if the item has not<br>changed since.|
|boxapi|header|string|false|The URL, and optional password, for the shared link of this item.<br><br>This header can be used to access items that have not been<br>explicitly shared with a user.<br><br>Use the format `shared_link=[link]` or if a password is required then<br>use `shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`.<br><br>This header can be used on the file or folder shared, as well as on any files<br>or folders nested within the item.|
|sort|query|string|false|Defines the **second** attribute by which items<br>are sorted.<br><br>The folder type affects the way the items<br>are sorted:<br><br>  * **Standard folder**:<br>  Items are always sorted by<br>  their `type` first, with<br>  folders listed before files,<br>  and files listed<br>  before web links.<br><br>  * **Root folder**:<br>  This parameter is not supported<br>  for marker-based pagination<br>  on the root folder<br><br>  (the folder with an `id` of `0`).<br><br>  * **Shared folder with parent path<br>  to the associated folder visible to<br>  the collaborator**:<br>  Items are always sorted by<br>  their `type` first, with<br>  folders listed before files,<br>  and files listed<br>  before web links.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort results in. This can be either in alphabetical ascending<br>(`ASC`) or descending (`DESC`) order.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Offset-based pagination is not guaranteed to work reliably for high offset values and may fail for large datasets. In<br>those cases, reduce the number of items in the folder (for example, by<br>restructuring the folder into smaller subfolders) before retrying the<br>request.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|id|
|sort|name|
|sort|date|
|sort|size|
|direction|ASC|
|direction|DESC|

<h3 id="get-folder-information-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a folder, including the first 100 entries in the folder.<br>If you used query parameters like<br>`sort`, `direction`, `offset`, or `limit`<br>the *folder items list* will be affected accordingly.<br><br>To fetch more items within the folder, use the<br>[Get items in a folder](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-folders-id-items)) endpoint.<br><br>Not all available fields are returned by default. Use the<br>[fields](#parameter-fields) query parameter to explicitly request<br>any specific fields.|[Folder--Full](#schemafolder--full)|
|304|Not Modified|Returns an empty response when the `If-None-Match` header matches<br>the current `etag` value of the folder. This indicates that the folder<br>has not changed since it was last requested.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned when the access token provided in the `Authorization` header<br>is not recognized or not provided.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the folder is not found, or the user does not<br>have access to the folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Returned if the `folder_id` is not in a recognized format.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Update folder

<a id="opIdput_folders_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/12345 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "New Folder",
    "description": "Legal contracts for the new ACME deal",
    "sync_state": "synced",
    "can_non_owners_invite": true,
    "parent": {
      "id": "123",
      "user_id": "12346930"
    },
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "permissions": {
        "can_download": true
      },
      "one_time_passcode": {
        "mode": "none"
      }
    },
    "folder_upload_email": {
      "access": "open"
    },
    "tags": [
      "approved"
    ],
    "is_collaboration_restricted_to_enterprise": true,
    "collections": [
      {
        "id": "11446498",
        "type": "file"
      }
    ],
    "can_non_owners_view_collaborators": true
  }'
```

`PUT /folders/{folder_id}`

Updates a folder. This can be also be used to move the folder,
create shared links, update collaborations, and more.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "New Folder",
  "description": "Legal contracts for the new ACME deal",
  "sync_state": "synced",
  "can_non_owners_invite": true,
  "parent": {
    "id": "123",
    "user_id": "12346930"
  },
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true
    },
    "one_time_passcode": {
      "mode": "none"
    }
  },
  "folder_upload_email": {
    "access": "open"
  },
  "tags": [
    "approved"
  ],
  "is_collaboration_restricted_to_enterprise": true,
  "collections": [
    {
      "id": "11446498",
      "type": "file"
    }
  ],
  "can_non_owners_view_collaborators": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The optional new name for this folder.<br><br>The following restrictions to folder names apply: names containing<br>non-printable ASCII characters, forward and backward slashes<br>(`/`, `\`), names with trailing spaces, and names `.` and `..` are<br>not allowed.<br><br>Folder names must be unique within their parent folder. The name check is case-insensitive,<br>so a folder named `New Folder` cannot be created in a parent folder that already contains<br>a folder named `new folder`.|
|» description|body|string|false|The optional description of this folder.|
|» sync_state|body|string|false|Specifies whether a folder should be synced to a<br>user's device or not. This is used by Box Sync<br>(discontinued) and is not used by Box Drive.|
|» can_non_owners_invite|body|boolean|false|Specifies if users who are not the owner<br>of the folder can invite new collaborators to the folder.|
|» parent|body|object|false|none|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of parent item.|
|» » user_id|body|string|false|The input for `user_id` is optional. Moving to non-root folder is not allowed when `user_id` is present. Parent folder id should be zero when `user_id` is provided.|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|none|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string \| null|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br>Passwords must now be at least eight characters<br>long and include a number, upper case letter, or<br>a non-numeric or non-alphabetic character.<br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared links.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » one_time_passcode|body|object|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableNone](#schemasharedlinkotpwritablenone)|false|One-time-passcode (OTP) enforcement is turned off. The shared link is<br>accessible without any one-time-passcode verification.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableOpen](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableopen)|false|Any anonymous recipient can request a one-time-passcode to any email<br>address and access the shared link after verifying it. Collaborators<br>and registered Box users access the link without being prompted.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableAllowlist](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableallowlist)|false|Anonymous recipients can request a one-time-passcode only when they<br>enter an email that matches an entry on the `allowlist`.|
|» folder_upload_email|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » access|body|string|false|When this parameter has been set, users can email files<br>to the email address that has been automatically<br>created for this folder.<br><br>To create an email address, set this property either when<br>creating or updating the folder.<br><br>When set to `collaborators`, only emails from registered email<br>addresses for collaborators will be accepted. This includes<br>any email aliases a user might have registered.<br><br>When set to `open` it will accept emails from any email<br>address.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|The tags for this item. These tags are shown in<br>the Box web app and mobile apps next to an item.<br><br>To add or remove a tag, retrieve the item's current tags,<br>modify them, and then update this field.<br><br>There is a limit of 100 tags per item, and 10,000<br>unique tags per enterprise.|
|» is_collaboration_restricted_to_enterprise|body|boolean|false|Specifies if new invites to this folder are restricted to users<br>within the enterprise. This does not affect existing<br>collaborations.|
|» collections|body|[object]|false|An array of collections to make this folder<br>a member of. Currently<br>we only support the `favorites` collection.<br><br>To get the ID for a collection, use the<br>[List all collections][1] endpoint.<br><br>Passing an empty array `[]` or `null` will remove<br>the folder from all collections.<br><br>[1]: https://developer.box.com/reference/get-collections|
|» » id|body|string|false|The unique identifier for this object.|
|» » type|body|string|false|The type for this object.|
|» can_non_owners_view_collaborators|body|boolean|false|Restricts collaborators who are not the owner of<br>this folder from viewing other collaborations on<br>this folder.<br><br>It also restricts non-owners from inviting new<br>collaborators.<br><br>When setting this field to `false`, it is required<br>to also set `can_non_owners_invite_collaborators` to<br>`false` if it has not already been set.|

<h3 id="update-folder-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a folder object for the updated folder<br><br>Not all available fields are returned by default. Use the<br>[fields](#parameter-fields) query parameter to explicitly request<br>any specific fields.<br><br>If the user is moving folders with a large number of items in all of<br>their descendants, the call will be run asynchronously. If the<br>operation is not completed within 10 minutes, the user will receive<br>a 200 OK response, and the operation will continue running.|[Folder--Full](#schemafolder--full)|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if some of the parameters are missing or<br>not valid, or if a folder lock is preventing a move operation.<br><br>* `bad_request` when a parameter is missing or incorrect. This error also<br>  happens when a password is set for a shared link with an access type<br>  of `open`.<br>* `item_name_too_long` when the folder name is too long.<br>* `item_name_invalid` when the folder name contains<br>  non-valid characters.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns an error if the user does not have the required<br>access to perform the action.<br><br>* `access_denied_insufficient_permissions`: Returned when the<br>  user does not have access to the folder or parent folder, or if the<br>  folder is being moved and a folder lock has been applied to prevent<br>  such operations.<br><br>* `insufficient_scope`: Returned an error if the application<br>  does not have the right scope to update folders. Make sure<br>  your application has been configured to read and write all files<br>  and folders stored in Box.<br><br>* `forbidden`: Returned when the user is not allowed to perform this<br>  action for other users. This can include trying to create a<br>  Shared Link with a `company` access level on a free account.<br><br>* `forbidden_by_policy`: Returned if copying a folder is<br>   forbidden due to information barrier restrictions.<br><br>Returns an error if there are too many actions in the request body.<br><br>* `operation_limit_exceeded`: Returned when the user passes any<br>parameters in addition to the `parent.id` in the request body.<br>The calls to this endpoint have to be split up.<br>The first call needs to include only the `parent.id`,<br>the next call can include other parameters.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error if the folder or parent folder could not be found,<br>or the authenticated user does not have access to either folder.<br><br>* `not_found` when the authenticated user does not have access<br>  to the folder or parent folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|`operation_blocked_temporary`: Returned if either of the destination<br>or source folders is locked due to another move, copy, delete or<br>restore operation in progress.<br><br>The operation can be retried at a later point.<br><br>`item_name_in_use`: Returned if a folder with the name<br>already exists in the parent folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|412|Precondition Failed|Returns an error when the `If-Match` header does not match<br>the current `etag` value of the folder. This indicates that the<br>folder has changed since it was last requested.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Returns an error when the operation takes longer<br>than 600 seconds. The operation will continue after<br>this response has been returned.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Delete folder

<a id="opIddelete_folders_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/12345 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /folders/{folder_id}`

Deletes a folder, either permanently or by moving it to
the trash.

<h3 id="delete-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|
|recursive|query|boolean|false|Delete a folder that is not empty by recursively deleting the<br>folder and all of its content.|

<h3 id="delete-folder-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returns an empty response when the folder is successfully deleted<br>or moved to the trash.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if the user makes a bad request.<br><br>* `folder_not_empty`: Returned if the folder is not empty. Use the<br>  `recursive` query parameter to recursively delete the folder and<br>  its contents.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns an error if the user does not have the required<br>access to perform the action.<br><br>* `access_denied_insufficient_permissions`: Returned when the<br>  user does not have access to the folder, or when a folder lock has been<br>  applied to the folder to prevent deletion.<br><br>* `insufficient_scope`: Returned an error if the application<br>  does not have the right scope to delete folders. Make sure<br>  your application has been configured to read and write all files<br>  and folders stored in Box.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error if the folder could not be found,<br>or the authenticated user does not have access to the folder.<br><br>* `not_found` when the authenticated user does not have access<br>  to the folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|`operation_blocked_temporary`: Returned if the folder<br>is locked due to another move, copy, delete or restore<br>operation in progress.<br><br>The operation can be retried at a later point.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|412|Precondition Failed|Returns an error when the `If-Match` header does not match<br>the current `etag` value of the folder. This indicates that the<br>folder has changed since it was last requested.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Returns an error when the operation takes longer<br>than 600 seconds. The operation will continue after<br>this response has been returned.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

## List items in folder

<a id="opIdget_folders_id_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/12345/items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /folders/{folder_id}/items`

Retrieves a page of items in a folder. These items can be files,
folders, and web links.

To request more information about the folder itself, like its size,
use the [Get a folder](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-folders-id) endpoint instead.

<h3 id="list-items-in-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.<br><br>Additionally this field can be used to query any metadata<br>applied to the file by specifying the `metadata` field as well<br>as the scope and key of the template to retrieve, for example<br>`?fields=metadata.enterprise_12345.contractTemplate`.|
|usemarker|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether to use marker-based pagination instead of<br>offset-based pagination. Only one pagination method can<br>be used at a time.<br><br>By setting this value to true, the API will return a `marker` field<br>that can be passed as a parameter to this endpoint to get the next<br>page of the response.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Offset-based pagination is not guaranteed to work reliably for high offset values and may fail for large datasets. In<br>those cases, use marker-based pagination by setting `usemarker` to `true`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|boxapi|header|string|false|The URL, and optional password, for the shared link of this item.<br><br>This header can be used to access items that have not been<br>explicitly shared with a user.<br><br>Use the format `shared_link=[link]` or if a password is required then<br>use `shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`.<br><br>This header can be used on the file or folder shared, as well as on any files<br>or folders nested within the item.|
|sort|query|string|false|Defines the **second** attribute by which items<br>are sorted.<br><br>The folder type affects the way the items<br>are sorted:<br><br>  * **Standard folder**:<br>  Items are always sorted by<br>  their `type` first, with<br>  folders listed before files,<br>  and files listed<br>  before web links.<br><br>  * **Root folder**:<br>  This parameter is not supported<br>  for marker-based pagination<br>  on the root folder<br><br>  (the folder with an `id` of `0`).<br><br>  * **Shared folder with parent path<br>  to the associated folder visible to<br>  the collaborator**:<br>  Items are always sorted by<br>  their `type` first, with<br>  folders listed before files,<br>  and files listed<br>  before web links.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort results in. This can be either in alphabetical ascending<br>(`ASC`) or descending (`DESC`) order.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|id|
|sort|name|
|sort|date|
|sort|size|
|direction|ASC|
|direction|DESC|
