<h3 id="list-items-in-folder-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a collection of files, folders, and web links contained in a folder.|[Items](#schemaitems)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned when the access token provided in the `Authorization` header<br>is not recognized or not provided.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the folder is not found, or the user does not<br>have access to the folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Returned if the `folder_id` is not in a recognized format.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Create folder

<a id="opIdpost_folders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/folders \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "New Folder",
    "parent": {
      "id": "0"
    },
    "folder_upload_email": {
      "access": "open"
    },
    "sync_state": "synced"
  }'
```

`POST /folders`

Creates a new empty folder within the specified parent folder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "New Folder",
  "parent": {
    "id": "0"
  },
  "folder_upload_email": {
    "access": "open"
  },
  "sync_state": "synced"
}
```

<h3 id="create-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name for the new folder.<br><br>The following restrictions to folder names apply: names containing<br>non-printable ASCII characters, forward and backward slashes<br>(`/`, `\`), names with trailing spaces, and names `.` and `..` are<br>not allowed.<br><br>Folder names must be unique within their parent folder. The name check is case-insensitive,<br>so a folder named `New Folder` cannot be created in a parent folder that already contains<br>a folder named `new folder`.|
|» parent|body|object|true|The parent folder to create the new folder within.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of parent folder.|
|» folder_upload_email|body|object|false|none|
|» » access|body|string|false|When this parameter has been set, users can email files<br>to the email address that has been automatically<br>created for this folder.<br><br>To create an email address, set this property either when<br>creating or updating the folder.<br><br>When set to `collaborators`, only emails from registered email<br>addresses for collaborators will be accepted. This includes<br>any email aliases a user might have registered.<br><br>When set to `open` it will accept emails from any email<br>address.|
|» sync_state|body|string|false|Specifies whether a folder should be synced to a<br>user's device or not. This is used by Box Sync<br>(discontinued) and is not used by Box Drive.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|collaborators|
|» sync_state|synced|
|» sync_state|not_synced|
|» sync_state|partially_synced|

<h3 id="create-folder-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returns a folder object.<br><br>Not all available fields are returned by default. Use the<br>[fields](#parameter-fields) query parameter to explicitly request<br>any specific fields.|[Folder--Full](#schemafolder--full)|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if some of the parameters are missing or<br>not valid.<br><br>* `bad_request` when a parameter is missing or incorrect.<br>* `item_name_too_long` when the folder name is too long.<br>* `item_name_invalid` when the folder name contains<br>  non-valid characters.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns an error if the user does not have the required<br>access to perform the action. This might be because they<br>don't have access to the folder or parent folder, or because<br>the application does not have permission to write files and<br>folders.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error if the parent folder could not be found,<br>or the authenticated user does not have access to the parent<br>folder.<br><br>* `not_found` when the authenticated user does not have access<br>  to the parent folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|`operation_blocked_temporary`: Returned if either of the destination<br>or source folders is locked due to another move, copy, delete or<br>restore operation in process.<br><br>The operation can be retried at a later point.<br><br>`item_name_in_use`: Returned if a folder with the name<br>already exists in the parent folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Copy folder

<a id="opIdpost_folders_id_copy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/0/copy \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "New Folder",
    "parent": {
      "id": "0"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /folders/{folder_id}/copy`

Creates a copy of a folder within a destination folder.

The original folder will not be changed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "New Folder",
  "parent": {
    "id": "0"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="copy-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the folder to copy.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder with the ID `0` can not be copied.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|An optional new name for the copied folder.<br><br>There are some restrictions to the file name. Names containing<br>non-printable ASCII characters, forward and backward slashes<br>(`/`, `\`), as well as names with trailing spaces are<br>prohibited.<br><br>Additionally, the names `.` and `..` are<br>not allowed either.|
|» parent|body|object|true|The destination folder to copy the folder to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of parent folder.|

<h3 id="copy-folder-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returns a new folder object representing the copied folder.<br><br>Not all available fields are returned by default. Use the<br>[fields](#parameter-fields) query parameter to explicitly request<br>any specific fields.|[Folder--Full](#schemafolder--full)|
|304|Not Modified|Returns an empty response when the `If-None-Match` header matches<br>the current `etag` value of the folder. This indicates that the folder<br>has not changed since it was last requested.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if some of the parameters are missing or<br>not valid.<br><br>* `bad_request` when a parameter is missing.<br>* `item_name_too_long` when the new folder name is too long.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns an error when the user does not have the<br>right permissions to copy a folder.<br><br>* `forbidden_by_policy`: Returned if copying a folder is<br>forbidden due to information barrier restrictions.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error if either the source or destination folder<br>could not be found, or the authenticated user does not<br>have access to either folders.<br><br>* `not_found` when the authenticated user does not have access<br>  to the parent folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|Returns an error if a folder by this name already exists<br>in the destination folder, or if the destination folder<br>is locked.<br><br>* `item_name_in_use` when a folder with the same name already<br>  exists.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Returns an error when trying to copy the root folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

<h1 id="box-platform-api-integration-mappings">Integration mappings</h1>

Integration Mappings allow the users
to manage where content from partner apps is stored in Box.

## List Slack integration mappings

<a id="opIdget_integration_mappings_slack"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/integration_mappings/slack \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /integration_mappings/slack`

Lists [Slack integration mappings](https://support.box.com/hc/en-us/articles/4415585987859-Box-as-the-Content-Layer-for-Slack) in a users' enterprise.

You need Admin or Co-Admin role to
use this endpoint.

<h3 id="list-slack-integration-mappings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|partner_item_type|query|string|false|Mapped item type, for which the mapping should be returned.|
|partner_item_id|query|string|false|ID of the mapped item,<br>for which the mapping should be returned.|
|box_item_id|query|string|false|Box item ID, for which the mappings should be returned.|
|box_item_type|query|string|false|Box item type, for<br>which the mappings should be returned.|
|is_manually_created|query|boolean|false|Whether the mapping has been manually created.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|partner_item_type|channel|
|box_item_type|folder|

## Create Slack integration mapping

<a id="opIdpost_integration_mappings_slack"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/integration_mappings/slack \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "partner_item": {
      "type": "channel",
      "id": "C12378991223",
      "slack_workspace_id": "T12352314",
      "slack_org_id": "E1234567"
    },
    "box_item": {
      "type": "folder",
      "id": "1234567891"
    },
    "options": {
      "is_access_management_disabled": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /integration_mappings/slack`

Creates a [Slack integration mapping](https://support.box.com/hc/en-us/articles/4415585987859-Box-as-the-Content-Layer-for-Slack)
by mapping a Slack channel to a Box item.

You need Admin or Co-Admin role to
use this endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "partner_item": {
    "type": "channel",
    "id": "C12378991223",
    "slack_workspace_id": "T12352314",
    "slack_org_id": "E1234567"
  },
  "box_item": {
    "type": "folder",
    "id": "1234567891"
  },
  "options": {
    "is_access_management_disabled": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-slack-integration-mapping-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IntegrationMappingSlackCreateRequest](#schemaintegrationmappingslackcreaterequest)|false|none|
|» partner_item|body|object|true|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|Type of the mapped item referenced in `id`.|
|» » id|body|string|true|ID of the mapped item (of type referenced in `type`).|
|» » slack_workspace_id|body|string \| null|false|ID of the Slack workspace with which the item is associated. Use this parameter if Box for Slack is installed at a workspace level. Do not use `slack_org_id` at the same time.|
|» » slack_org_id|body|string \| null|false|ID of the Slack org with which the item is associated. Use this parameter if Box for Slack is installed at the org level. Do not use `slack_workspace_id` at the same time.|
|» box_item|body|object|true|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|Type of the mapped item referenced in `id`.|
|» » id|body|string|true|ID of the mapped item (of type referenced in `type`).|
|» options|body|object|false|none|
|» » is_access_management_disabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether or not channel member<br>access to the underlying box item<br>should be automatically managed.<br>Depending on type of channel, access is managed<br>through creating collaborations or shared links.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|channel|
|» » type|folder|

<h3 id="create-slack-integration-mapping-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returns the created integration mapping.|[IntegrationMapping](#schemaintegrationmapping)|
|400|Bad Request|Returns a `bad_request` if an incorrect `options`<br>was supplied or the Box folder cannot be<br>mapped to this `partner_item_id`.<br>Error codes:<br>* `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_IS_NOT_A_COOWNER_OR_OWNER` - service account<br>doesn't have co-owner collaboration or is<br>not an owner of the `box_item_id`,<br>* `CHANNEL_ALREADY_MAPPED` - channel is already<br>  mapped to another `box_item_id`,<br>* `CHANNEL_NOT_FOUND` - channel was not found,<br>* `CHANNEL_NOT_SUITABLE_FOR_CFS` - connect channel, not<br>suitable for Box as Content layer for Slack,<br>* `BOX_ENTERPRISE_MISMATCH` - Box folder must be<br>owned by the enterprise, which is configured<br>to use Box as Content layer for Slack,<br>* `CFS_DISABLED` - Box as Content layer<br>for Slack must be enabled for a provided<br>Slack workspace or organization<br>* `BOX_FOLDER_EXTERNALLY_OWNED` - Box folder must<br>be internally owned to the admin's enterprise,<br>* `JWT_APP_NOT_AUTHORIZED` - JWT authorization error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns a `not_found` error if the integration mapping could not be found.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

`PUT /integration_mappings/slack/{integration_mapping_id}`

Updates a [Slack integration mapping](https://support.box.com/hc/en-us/articles/4415585987859-Box-as-the-Content-Layer-for-Slack).
Supports updating the Box folder ID and options.

You need Admin or Co-Admin role to
use this endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "box_item": {
    "type": "folder",
    "id": "1234567891"
  },
  "options": {
    "is_access_management_disabled": true
  }
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|object|false|At least one of `box_item` and `options` must be provided.|
|» box_item|body|object|false|none|

|» » id|body|string|true|ID of the mapped item (of type referenced in `type`).|

`POST /integration_mappings/teams`

{
  "partner_item": {
    "type": "channel",

  }

<h3 id="create-teams-integration-mapping-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IntegrationMappingTeamsCreateRequest](#schemaintegrationmappingteamscreaterequest)|false|none|
|» partner_item|body|object|true|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|Type of the mapped item referenced in `id`.|
|» » id|body|string|true|ID of the mapped item (of type referenced in `type`).|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-group-memberships">Group memberships</h1>

Group memberships signify that
a user is a part of the group.

<a id="opIdget_users_id_memberships"></a>

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"

`GET /users/{user_id}/memberships`

Retrieves all the groups for a user. Only members of this

use this API.

## Add user to group

<a id="opIdpost_group_memberships"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/group_memberships \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \

    },

    "configurable_permissions": {
      "can_run_reports": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /group_memberships`

Creates a group membership. Only users with
admin-level permissions will be able to use this API.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user": {
    "id": "1434325"
  },
  "group": {
    "id": "4545523"
  },
  "role": "member",
  "configurable_permissions": {
    "can_run_reports": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-user-to-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» user|body|object|true|The user to add to the group.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the user to add to the group.|
|» group|body|object|true|The group to add the user to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the group to add the user to.|
|» role|body|string|false|The role of the user in the group.|
|» configurable_permissions|body|object \| null|false|Custom configuration for the permissions an admin<br>if a group will receive. This option has no effect<br>on members with a role of `member`.<br><br>Setting these permissions overwrites the default<br>access levels of an admin.<br><br>Specifying a value of `null` for this object will disable<br>all configurable permissions. Specifying permissions will set<br>them accordingly, omitted permissions will be enabled by default.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|boolean|false|A key value pair of custom permissions.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

|» role|admin|

## Create group

<a id="opIdpost_groups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/groups \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Customer Support",
    "provenance": "Active Directory",
    "external_sync_identifier": "AD:123456",
    "description": "\"Customer Support Group - as imported from Active Directory\"",
    "invitability_level": "admins_only",
    "member_viewability_level": "admins_only"
  }'
```

`POST /groups`

Creates a new group of users in an enterprise. Only users with admin
permissions can create new groups.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Customer Support",
  "provenance": "Active Directory",
  "external_sync_identifier": "AD:123456",
  "description": "\"Customer Support Group - as imported from Active Directory\"",
  "invitability_level": "admins_only",
  "member_viewability_level": "admins_only"
}
```

<h3 id="create-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the new group to be created. This name must be unique<br>within the enterprise.|
|» provenance|body|string|false|Keeps track of which external source this group is<br>coming, for example `Active Directory`, or `Okta`.<br><br>Setting this will also prevent Box admins from editing<br>the group name and its members directly via the Box<br>web application.<br><br>This is desirable for one-way syncing of groups.|
|» external_sync_identifier|body|string|false|An arbitrary identifier that can be used by<br>external group sync tools to link this Box Group to<br>an external group.<br><br>Example values of this field<br>could be an **Active Directory Object ID** or a **Google<br>Group ID**.<br><br>We recommend you use of this field in<br>order to avoid issues when group names are updated in<br>either Box or external systems.|
|» description|body|string|false|A human readable description of the group.|
|» invitability_level|body|string|false|Specifies who can invite the group to collaborate<br>on folders.<br><br>When set to `admins_only` the enterprise admin, co-admins,<br>and the group's admin can invite the group.<br><br>When set to `admins_and_members` all the admins listed<br>above and group members can invite the group.<br><br>When set to `all_managed_users` all managed users in the<br>enterprise can invite the group.|
|» member_viewability_level|body|string|false|Specifies who can see the members of the group.<br><br>* `admins_only` - the enterprise admin, co-admins, group's<br>  group admin.<br>* `admins_and_members` - all admins and group members.<br>* `all_managed_users` - all managed users in the<br>  enterprise.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» invitability_level|admins_only|
|» invitability_level|admins_and_members|
|» invitability_level|all_managed_users|
|» member_viewability_level|admins_only|
|» member_viewability_level|admins_and_members|
|» member_viewability_level|all_managed_users|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-invites">Invites</h1>

Invites are used to invite the user to
an enterprise.

## Create user invite

<a id="opIdpost_invites"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/invites \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "enterprise": {
      "id": "1232234"
    },
    "actionable_by": {
      "login": "john@example.com"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /invites`

Invites an existing external user to join an enterprise.

The existing user can not be part of another enterprise and
must already have a Box account. Once invited, the user will receive an
email and are prompted to accept the invitation within the
Box web application.

This method requires the "Manage An Enterprise" scope enabled for
the application, which can be enabled within the developer console.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enterprise": {
    "id": "1232234"
  },
  "actionable_by": {
    "login": "john@example.com"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-user-invite-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» enterprise|body|object|true|The enterprise to invite the user to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the enterprise.|
|» actionable_by|body|object|true|The user to invite.|
|» » login|body|string|false|The login of the invited user.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "11446498",
  "type": "invite",
  "invited_to": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "enterprise",
    "name": "Acme Inc."
  },
  "actionable_by": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "user",
    "name": "Aaron Levie",
    "login": "ceo@example.com"
  },
  "invited_by": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "user",
    "name": "Aaron Levie",
    "login": "ceo@example.com"
  },
  "status": "pending",
  "created_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",

}

<h1 id="box-platform-api-legal-hold-policies">Legal hold policies</h1>

A legal hold is a process that an enterprise
can use to preserve all forms of potentially
relevant information when litigation is pending or
reasonably anticipated.

## List all legal hold policies

<a id="opIdget_legal_hold_policies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"

## Create legal hold policy

<a id="opIdpost_legal_hold_policies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/legal_hold_policies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "policy_name": "Sales Policy",
    "description": "A custom policy for the sales team",
    "filter_started_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "filter_ended_at": "2012-12-18T10:53:43-08:00",
    "is_ongoing": true
  }'
```

`POST /legal_hold_policies`

Create a new legal hold policy.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "policy_name": "Sales Policy",
  "description": "A custom policy for the sales team",
  "filter_started_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "filter_ended_at": "2012-12-18T10:53:43-08:00",
  "is_ongoing": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-legal-hold-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» policy_name|body|string|true|The name of the policy.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description for the policy.|
|» filter_started_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The filter start date.<br><br>When this policy is applied using a `custodian` legal<br>hold assignments, it will only apply to file versions<br>created or uploaded inside of the<br>date range. Other assignment types, such as folders and<br>files, will ignore the date filter.<br><br>Required if `is_ongoing` is set to `false`.|
|» filter_ended_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The filter end date.<br><br>When this policy is applied using a `custodian` legal<br>hold assignments, it will only apply to file versions<br>created or uploaded inside of the<br>date range. Other assignment types, such as folders and<br>files, will ignore the date filter.<br><br>Required if `is_ongoing` is set to `false`.|
|» is_ongoing|body|boolean|false|Whether new assignments under this policy should<br>continue applying to files even after initialization.<br><br>When this policy is applied using a legal hold assignment,<br>it will continue applying the policy to any new file versions<br>even after it has been applied.<br><br>For example, if a legal hold assignment is placed on a user<br>today, and that user uploads a file tomorrow, that file will<br>get held. This will continue until the policy is retired.<br><br>Required if no filter dates are set.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-legal-hold-policy-assignments">Legal hold policy assignments</h1>

A Legal Hold Policy Assignment
is a relation between a policy and custodian.
In this case, as custodian can be a user, folder,
file, or file version.

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

## List files with current file versions for legal hold policy assignment

<a id="opIdget_legal_hold_policy_assignments_id_files_on_hold"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/legal_hold_policy_assignments/753465/files_on_hold \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments/{legal_hold_policy_assignment_id}/files_on_hold`

Get a list of files with current file versions for a legal hold
assignment.

In some cases you may want to get previous file versions instead. In these
cases, use the `GET  /legal_hold_policy_assignments/:id/file_versions_on_hold`
API instead to return any previous versions of a file for this legal hold
policy assignment.

Due to ongoing re-architecture efforts this API might not return all file
versions held for this policy ID. Instead, this API will only return the
latest file version held in the newly developed architecture. The `GET
/file_version_legal_holds` API can be used to fetch current and past versions
of files held within the legacy architecture.

This endpoint does not support returning any content that is on hold due to
a Custodian collaborating on a Hub.

The `GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments?policy_id={id}` API can be used to
find a list of policy assignments for a given policy ID.

<h1 id="box-platform-api-metadata-cascade-policies">Metadata cascade policies</h1>

A metadata cascade policy describes how metadata
instances applied to a folder should be applied
to any item within that folder.

## List metadata cascade policies

<a id="opIdget_metadata_cascade_policies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/metadata_cascade_policies?folder_id=31232' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /metadata_cascade_policies`

Retrieves a list of all the metadata cascade policies
that are applied to a given folder. This can not be used on the root
folder with ID `0`.

<h3 id="list-metadata-cascade-policies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|folder_id|query|string|true|Specifies which folder to return policies for. This can not be used on the<br>root folder with ID `0`.|

|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|

## Create metadata cascade policy

<a id="opIdpost_metadata_cascade_policies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/metadata_cascade_policies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "folder_id": "1234567",
    "scope": "enterprise",
    "templateKey": "productInfo"
  }'
```

`POST /metadata_cascade_policies`

Creates a new metadata cascade policy that applies a given
metadata template to a given folder and automatically
cascades it down to any files within that folder.

In order for the policy to be applied a metadata instance must first
be applied to the folder the policy is to be applied to.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "folder_id": "1234567",
  "scope": "enterprise",
  "templateKey": "productInfo"
}
```

<h3 id="create-metadata-cascade-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» folder_id|body|string|true|The ID of the folder to apply the policy to. This folder will<br>need to already have an instance of the targeted metadata<br>template applied to it.|
|» scope|body|string|true|The scope of the targeted metadata template. This template will<br>need to already have an instance applied to the targeted folder.|
|» templateKey|body|string|true|The key of the targeted metadata template. This template will<br>need to already have an instance applied to the targeted folder.<br><br>In many cases the template key is automatically derived<br>of its display name, for example `Contract Template` would<br>become `contractTemplate`. In some cases the creator of the<br>template will have provided its own template key.<br><br>Please [list the templates for an enterprise][list], or<br>get all instances on a [file][file] or [folder][folder]<br>to inspect a template's key.<br><br>[list]: https://developer.box.com/reference/get-metadata-templates-enterprise<br>[file]: https://developer.box.com/reference/get-files-id-metadata<br>[folder]: https://developer.box.com/reference/get-folders-id-metadata|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» scope|global|
|» scope|enterprise|

    "type": "enterprise",
    "id": "690678"
  },

    "type": "folder",

  },

}

|400|Bad Request|Returns an error when any of the parameters are not in a valid format.<br><br>* `bad_request` - Either the `scope`, `templateKey`, or `folder_id` are<br>not in a valid format.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns an error when trying to apply a policy to a restricted folder, for<br>example the root folder with ID `0`.<br><br>* `forbidden` - Although the folder ID was valid and the user has access<br>to the folder, the policy could not be applied to this folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error when the template or folder can not be found, or when the<br>user does not have access to the folder or template.<br><br>* `instance_tuple_not_found` - The template could not be found or the user<br>does not have access to the template.<br>* `not_found` - The folder could not be found or the user<br>does not have access to the folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|Returns an error when a policy for this folder and template is already in<br>place.<br><br>* `tuple_already_exists` - A cascade policy for this combination of<br>`folder_id`, `scope` and `templateKey` already exists.|[ConflictError](#schemaconflicterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

## Force-apply metadata cascade policy to folder

<a id="opIdpost_metadata_cascade_policies_id_apply"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/metadata_cascade_policies/6fd4ff89-8fc1-42cf-8b29-1890dedd26d7/apply \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conflict_resolution": "none"
  }'
```

`POST /metadata_cascade_policies/{metadata_cascade_policy_id}/apply`

Force the metadata on a folder with a metadata cascade policy to be applied to
all of its children. This can be used after creating a new cascade policy to
enforce the metadata to be cascaded down to all existing files within that
folder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conflict_resolution": "none"
}
```

<h3 id="force-apply-metadata-cascade-policy-to-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|metadata_cascade_policy_id|path|string|true|The ID of the cascade policy to force-apply.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» conflict_resolution|body|string|true|Describes the desired behavior when dealing with the conflict<br>where a metadata template already has an instance applied<br>to a child.<br><br>* `none` will preserve the existing value on the file<br>* `overwrite` will force-apply the templates values over<br>  any existing values.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» conflict_resolution|none|
|» conflict_resolution|overwrite|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-metadata-instances-files">Metadata instances (Files)</h1>

A metadata instance describes
the relation between a template and a file,
including the values that are assigned for every field.

## Update metadata instance on file

<a id="opIdput_files_id_metadata_id_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345/metadata/global/properties \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json-patch+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "op": "add",
      "path": "/currentState",
      "value": "reviewed",
      "from": "/nextState"
    }
  ]'
```

`PUT /files/{file_id}/metadata/{scope}/{template_key}`

Updates a piece of metadata on a file.

The metadata instance can only be updated if the template has already been
applied to the file before. When editing metadata, only values that match
the metadata template schema will be accepted.

The update is applied atomically. If any errors occur during the
application of the operations, the metadata instance will not be changed.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "op": "add",
    "path": "/currentState",
    "value": "reviewed",
    "from": "/nextState"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="update-metadata-instance-on-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|scope|path|string|true|The scope of the metadata template.|
|template_key|path|string|true|The name of the metadata template.|
|body|body|[object]|false|none|
|» op|body|string|false|The type of change to perform on the template. Some<br>of these are hazardous as they will change existing templates.|
|» path|body|string|false|The location in the metadata JSON object<br>to apply the changes to, in the format of a<br>[JSON-Pointer](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901).<br><br>The path must always be prefixed with a `/` to represent the root<br>of the template. The characters `~` and `/` are reserved<br>characters and must be escaped in the key.|
|» value|body|[MetadataInstanceValue](#schemametadatainstancevalue)|false|The value to be set or tested.<br><br>Required for `add`, `replace`, and `test` operations. For `add`,<br>if the value exists already the previous value will be overwritten<br>by the new value. For `replace`, the value must exist before<br>replacing.<br><br>For `test`, the existing value at the `path` location must match<br>the specified value.|
|» from|body|string|false|The location in the metadata JSON object to move or copy a value<br>from. Required for `move` or `copy` operations and must be in the<br>format of a [JSON-Pointer](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|global|
|scope|enterprise|
|» op|add|
|» op|replace|
|» op|remove|
|» op|test|
|» op|move|
|» op|copy|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "$parent": "folder_59449484661,",
  "$template": "marketingCollateral",
  "$scope": "enterprise_27335",
  "$version": 1,
  "$canEdit": true,
  "$id": "01234500-12f1-1234-aa12-b1d234cb567e",
  "$type": "properties-6bcba49f-ca6d-4d2a-a758-57fe6edf44d0",

  "property2": {}
}

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|201|Created|Returns the instance of the template that was applied to the file,<br>including the data that was applied to the template.|[Metadata--Full](#schemametadata--full)|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error when the request body is not valid.<br><br>* `schema_validation_failed` - The request body contains a value for<br>a field that either does not exist, or for which the value or type does<br>not match the expected field type. An example might be an unknown option<br>for an `enum` or `multiSelect` field.|[MetadataError](#schemametadataerror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error when the file or metadata template was not found.<br><br>* `not_found` - The file could not be found, or the user does not have<br>access to the file.<br>* `instance_tuple_not_found` - The metadata template was not found.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|Returns an error when an instance of this metadata template is already<br>present on the file.<br><br>* `tuple_already_exists` - An instance of the metadata template already<br>exists on the file.|[MetadataError](#schemametadataerror)|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-metadata-instances-folders">Metadata instances (Folders)</h1>

A metadata instance describes the relation between a template and a folder,
including the values that are assigned for every field.

## Update metadata instance on folder

<a id="opIdput_folders_id_metadata_id_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/12345/metadata/global/properties \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json-patch+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "op": "add",
      "path": "/currentState",
      "value": "reviewed",
      "from": "/nextState"
    }
  ]'
```

`PUT /folders/{folder_id}/metadata/{scope}/{template_key}`

Updates a piece of metadata on a folder.

The metadata instance can only be updated if the template has already been
applied to the folder before. When editing metadata, only values that match
the metadata template schema will be accepted.

The update is applied atomically. If any errors occur during the
application of the operations, the metadata instance will not be changed.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "op": "add",
    "path": "/currentState",
    "value": "reviewed",
    "from": "/nextState"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="update-metadata-instance-on-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|scope|path|string|true|The scope of the metadata template.|
|template_key|path|string|true|The name of the metadata template.|
|body|body|[object]|false|none|
|» op|body|string|false|The type of change to perform on the template. Some<br>of these are hazardous as they will change existing templates.|
|» path|body|string|false|The location in the metadata JSON object<br>to apply the changes to, in the format of a<br>[JSON-Pointer](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901).<br><br>The path must always be prefixed with a `/` to represent the root<br>of the template. The characters `~` and `/` are reserved<br>characters and must be escaped in the key.|
|» value|body|[MetadataInstanceValue](#schemametadatainstancevalue)|false|The value to be set or tested.<br><br>Required for `add`, `replace`, and `test` operations. For `add`,<br>if the value exists already the previous value will be overwritten<br>by the new value. For `replace`, the value must exist before<br>replacing.<br><br>For `test`, the existing value at the `path` location must match<br>the specified value.|
|» from|body|string|false|The location in the metadata JSON object to move or copy a value<br>from. Required for `move` or `copy` operations and must be in the<br>format of a [JSON-Pointer](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|global|
|scope|enterprise|
|» op|add|
|» op|replace|
|» op|remove|
|» op|test|
|» op|move|
|» op|copy|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "$parent": "folder_59449484661,",
  "$template": "marketingCollateral",
  "$scope": "enterprise_27335",
  "$version": 1,
  "$canEdit": true,
  "$id": "01234500-12f1-1234-aa12-b1d234cb567e",
  "$type": "properties-6bcba49f-ca6d-4d2a-a758-57fe6edf44d0",
  "$typeVersion": 2,
  "property1": {},
  "property2": {}
}
```

  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json

## Create metadata instance on folder

<a id="opIdpost_folders_id_metadata_id_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/12345/metadata/global/properties \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Aaron Levie"
  }'
```

`POST /folders/{folder_id}/metadata/{scope}/{template_key}`

Applies an instance of a metadata template to a folder.

In most cases only values that are present in the metadata template
will be accepted, except for the `global.properties` template which accepts
any key-value pair.

To display the metadata template in the Box web app the enterprise needs to be
configured to enable **Cascading Folder Level Metadata** for the user in the
admin console.

> Body parameter

{
  "name": "Aaron Levie"
}

For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|scope|path|string|true|The scope of the metadata template.|
|template_key|path|string|true|The name of the metadata template.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-metadata-taxonomies">Metadata taxonomies</h1>

A metadata taxonomy is a hierarchical classification system
that helps organize and manage metadata
within an enterprise.

## Create metadata taxonomy

<a id="opIdpost_metadata_taxonomies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/metadata_taxonomies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "key": "geography",
    "displayName": "Geography",
    "namespace": "enterprise_123456"
  }'
```

`POST /metadata_taxonomies`

Creates a new metadata taxonomy that can be used in
metadata templates.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "key": "geography",
  "displayName": "Geography",
  "namespace": "enterprise_123456"
}
```

<h3 id="create-metadata-taxonomy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» key|body|string|false|The taxonomy key. If it is not provided in the request body, it will be <br>generated from the `displayName`. The `displayName` would be converted <br>to lower case, and all spaces and non-alphanumeric characters replaced <br>with underscores.|
|» displayName|body|string|true|The display name of the taxonomy.|
|» namespace|body|string|true|The namespace of the metadata taxonomy to create.|

> Example responses

  "id": "822227e0-47a5-921b-88a8-494760b2e6d2",

## List metadata taxonomy nodes

<a id="opIdget_metadata_taxonomies_id_id_nodes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/metadata_taxonomies/enterprise_123456/geography/nodes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /metadata_taxonomies/{namespace}/{taxonomy_key}/nodes`

Used to retrieve metadata taxonomy nodes based on the parameters specified. 
Results are sorted in lexicographic order unless a `query` parameter is passed. 
With a `query` parameter specified, results are sorted in order of relevance.

<h3 id="list-metadata-taxonomy-nodes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|The namespace of the metadata taxonomy.|
|taxonomy_key|path|string|true|The key of the metadata taxonomy.|
|level|query|[integer]|false|Filters results by taxonomy level. Multiple values can be provided. <br>Results include nodes that match any of the specified values.|
|parent|query|[string]|false|Node identifier of a direct parent node. Multiple values can be provided. <br>Results include nodes that match any of the specified values.|
|ancestor|query|[string]|false|Node identifier of any ancestor node. Multiple values can be provided. <br>Results include nodes that match any of the specified values.|
|query|query|string|false|Query text to search for the taxonomy nodes.|
|include-total-result-count|query|boolean|false|When set to `true` this provides the total number of nodes that matched the query. <br>The response will compute counts of up to 10,000 elements. Defaults to `false`.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "limit": 1000,
  "next_marker": "JV9IRGZmieiBasejOG9yDCRNgd2ymoZIbjsxbJMjIs3kioVii",
  "prev_marker": "JV9IRGZmieiBasejOG9yDCRNgd2ymoZIbjsxbJMjIs3kioVih",
  "entries": [
    {
      "id": "14d3d433-c77f-49c5-b146-9dea370f6e32",
      "displayName": "France",
      "level": 2,
      "parentId": "99df4513-7102-4896-8228-94635ee9d330",
      "nodePath": [
        "99df4513-7102-4896-8228-94635ee9d330"
      ],
      "ancestors": [
        {
          "id": "14d3d433-c77f-49c5-b146-9dea370f6e32",
          "displayName": "France",
          "level": 2
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "context_info": {

  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",

|403|Forbidden|Returned when the user does not have the permission to modify the metadata<br>taxonomy. This can happen for a few reasons, most commonly when the user<br>does not have (co-)admin permissions, or the user doesn't have access to <br>the provided namespace.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

OAuth2Security

## List metadata template's options for taxonomy field

<a id="opIdget_metadata_templates_id_id_fields_id_options"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/metadata_templates/enterprise_123456/properties/fields/geography/options \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /metadata_templates/{namespace}/{template_key}/fields/{field_key}/options`

Used to retrieve metadata taxonomy nodes which are available for the taxonomy field based 
on its configuration and the parameters specified. 
Results are sorted in lexicographic order unless a `query` parameter is passed. 
With a `query` parameter specified, results are sorted in order of relevance.

<h3 id="list-metadata-templates-options-for-taxonomy-field-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|The namespace of the metadata taxonomy.|
|template_key|path|string|true|The name of the metadata template.|
|field_key|path|string|true|The key of the metadata taxonomy field in the template.|
|level|query|[integer]|false|Filters results by taxonomy level. Multiple values can be provided. <br>Results include nodes that match any of the specified values.|
|parent|query|[string]|false|Node identifier of a direct parent node. Multiple values can be provided. <br>Results include nodes that match any of the specified values.|
|ancestor|query|[string]|false|Node identifier of any ancestor node. Multiple values can be provided. <br>Results include nodes that match any of the specified values.|
|query|query|string|false|Query text to search for the taxonomy nodes.|
|include-total-result-count|query|boolean|false|When set to `true` this provides the total number of nodes that matched the query. <br>The response will compute counts of up to 10,000 elements. Defaults to `false`.|
|only-selectable-options|query|boolean|false|When set to `true`, this only returns valid selectable options for this template<br>taxonomy field. Otherwise, it returns all taxonomy nodes, whether or not they are selectable.<br>Defaults to `true`.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "limit": 1000,
  "next_marker": "JV9IRGZmieiBasejOG9yDCRNgd2ymoZIbjsxbJMjIs3kioVii",
  "prev_marker": "JV9IRGZmieiBasejOG9yDCRNgd2ymoZIbjsxbJMjIs3kioVih",
  "entries": [

      ],
      "ancestors": [
        {
          "id": "14d3d433-c77f-49c5-b146-9dea370f6e32",
          "displayName": "France",
          "level": 2
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="box-platform-api-metadata-templates">Metadata templates</h1>

A metadata template describes a reusable set
of key/value pairs that can be assigned to a file.

## Update metadata template

<a id="opIdput_metadata_templates_id_id_schema"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/metadata_templates/global/properties/schema \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json-patch+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "op": "addEnumOption",
      "data": {
        "name": "Aaron Levie"
      },
      "fieldKey": "category",
      "fieldKeys": [
        "category",
        "name"
      ],
      "enumOptionKey": "option1",
      "enumOptionKeys": [
        "option1",
        "option2",
        "option3"
      ],
      "multiSelectOptionKey": "option1",
      "multiSelectOptionKeys": [
        "option1",
        "option2",
        "option3"
      ]
    }
  ]'
```

`PUT /metadata_templates/{scope}/{template_key}/schema`

Updates a metadata template.

The metadata template can only be updated if the template
already exists.

The update is applied atomically. If any errors occur during the
application of the operations, the metadata template will not be changed.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "op": "addEnumOption",
    "data": {
      "name": "Aaron Levie"
    },
    "fieldKey": "category",
    "fieldKeys": [
      "category",
      "name"
    ],
    "enumOptionKey": "option1",
    "enumOptionKeys": [
      "option1",
      "option2",
      "option3"
    ],
    "multiSelectOptionKey": "option1",
    "multiSelectOptionKeys": [
      "option1",
      "option2",
      "option3"
    ]
  }
]
```

<h3 id="update-metadata-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scope|path|string|true|The scope of the metadata template.|
|template_key|path|string|true|The name of the metadata template.|
|body|body|[object]|false|none|
|» op|body|string|true|The type of change to perform on the template. Some<br>of these are hazardous as they will change existing templates.|
|» data|body|object|false|The data for the operation. This will vary depending on the<br>operation being performed.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» fieldKey|body|string|false|For operations that affect a single field this defines the key of<br>the field that is affected.|
|» fieldKeys|body|[string]|false|For operations that affect multiple fields this defines the keys<br>of the fields that are affected.|
|» enumOptionKey|body|string|false|For operations that affect a single `enum` option this defines<br>the key of the option that is affected.|
|» enumOptionKeys|body|[string]|false|For operations that affect multiple `enum` options this defines<br>the keys of the options that are affected.|
|» multiSelectOptionKey|body|string|false|For operations that affect a single multi select option this<br>defines the key of the option that is affected.|
|» multiSelectOptionKeys|body|[string]|false|For operations that affect multiple multi select options this<br>defines the keys of the options that are affected.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|global|
|scope|enterprise|
|» op|editTemplate|
|» op|addField|
|» op|reorderFields|
|» op|addEnumOption|
|» op|reorderEnumOptions|
|» op|reorderMultiSelectOptions|
|» op|addMultiSelectOption|
|» op|editField|
|» op|removeField|
|» op|editEnumOption|
|» op|removeEnumOption|
|» op|editMultiSelectOption|
|» op|removeMultiSelectOption|

## Create metadata template

<a id="opIdpost_metadata_templates_schema"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/metadata_templates/schema \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "scope": "enterprise",
    "templateKey": "productInfo",
    "displayName": "Product Info",
    "hidden": true,
    "fields": [
      {
        "type": "string",
        "key": "category",
        "displayName": "Category",
        "description": "The category",
        "hidden": true,
        "options": [
          {
            "key": "Category 1"
          }
        ],
        "taxonomyKey": "locationTaxonomy",
        "taxonomyId": "05ece6d7-fec4-4d3f-bfd2-36fd4dddea97",
        "namespace": "enterprise_123456",
        "optionsRules": {
          "multiSelect": true,
          "selectableLevels": [
            1,
            2
          ]
        }
      }
    ],
    "copyInstanceOnItemCopy": true
  }'
```

`POST /metadata_templates/schema`

Creates a new metadata template that can be applied to
files and folders.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "scope": "enterprise",
  "templateKey": "productInfo",
  "displayName": "Product Info",
  "hidden": true,
  "fields": [
    {
      "type": "string",
      "key": "category",
      "displayName": "Category",
      "description": "The category",
      "hidden": true,
      "options": [
        {
          "key": "Category 1"
        }
      ],
      "taxonomyKey": "locationTaxonomy",
      "taxonomyId": "05ece6d7-fec4-4d3f-bfd2-36fd4dddea97",
      "namespace": "enterprise_123456",
      "optionsRules": {
        "multiSelect": true,
        "selectableLevels": [
          1,
          2
        ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "copyInstanceOnItemCopy": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-metadata-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» scope|body|string|true|The scope of the metadata template to create. Applications can<br>only create templates for use within the authenticated user's<br>enterprise.<br><br>This value needs to be set to `enterprise`, as `global` scopes can<br>not be created by applications.|
|» templateKey|body|string|false|A unique identifier for the template. This identifier needs to be<br>unique across the enterprise for which the metadata template is<br>being created.<br><br>When not provided, the API will create a unique `templateKey`<br>based on the value of the `displayName`.|
|» displayName|body|string|true|The display name of the template.|
|» hidden|body|boolean|false|Defines if this template is visible in the Box web app UI, or if<br>it is purely intended for usage through the API.|
|» fields|body|[object]|false|An ordered list of template fields which are part of the template.<br>Each field can be a regular text field, date field, number field,<br>as well as a single or multi-select list.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of field. The basic fields are a `string` field for text, a<br>`float` field for numbers, and a `date` field to present the user with a<br>date-time picker.<br><br>Additionally, metadata templates support an `enum` field for a basic list<br>of items, and `multiSelect` field for a similar list of items where the<br>user can select more than one value.<br><br>Metadata taxonomies are also supported as a `taxonomy` field type <br>with a specific set of additional properties, which describe its structure.|
|» » key|body|string|true|A unique identifier for the field. The identifier must<br>be unique within the template to which it belongs.|
|» » displayName|body|string|true|The display name of the field as it is shown to the user in the web and<br>mobile apps.|
|» » description|body|string|false|A description of the field. This is not shown to the user.|
|» » hidden|body|boolean|false|Whether this field is hidden in the UI for the user and can only be set<br>through the API instead.|
|» » options|body|[object]|false|A list of options for this field. This is used in combination with the<br>`enum` and `multiSelect` field types.|
|» » » key|body|string|true|The text value of the option. This represents both the display name of the<br>option and the internal key used when updating templates.|
|» » taxonomyKey|body|string|false|The unique key of the metadata taxonomy to use for this taxonomy field.<br>This property is required when the field `type` is set to `taxonomy`.|
|» » taxonomyId|body|string|false|The unique ID of the metadata taxonomy to use for this taxonomy field.<br>This property is required when the field `type` is set to `taxonomy`.|
|» » namespace|body|string|false|The namespace of the metadata taxonomy to use for this taxonomy field.<br>This property is required when the field `type` is set to `taxonomy`.|
|» » optionsRules|body|object|false|An object defining additional rules for the options of the taxonomy field.<br>This property is required when the field `type` is set to `taxonomy`.|
|» » » multiSelect|body|boolean|false|Whether to allow users to select multiple values.|
|» » » selectableLevels|body|[integer]|false|An array of integers defining which levels of the taxonomy are<br>selectable by users.|
|» copyInstanceOnItemCopy|body|boolean|false|Whether or not to copy any metadata attached to a file or folder<br>when it is copied. By default, metadata is not copied along with a<br>file or folder when it is copied.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|string|
|» » type|float|
|» » type|date|
|» » type|enum|
|» » type|multiSelect|
|» » type|taxonomy|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "58063d82-4128-7b43-bba9-92f706befcdf",
  "type": "metadata_template",
  "scope": "enterprise_123456",
  "templateKey": "productInfo",
  "displayName": "Product Info",
  "hidden": true,
  "fields": [
    {
      "type": "string",
      "key": "category",

      "description": "The category",
      "hidden": true,

        {
          "key": "Category 1",

        }
      ],

      "namespace": "enterprise_123456",
      "optionsRules": {
        "multiSelect": true,
        "selectableLevels": [
          1,
          2
        ]
      },
      "id": "822227e0-47a5-921b-88a8-494760b2e6d2"
    }
  ],
  "copyInstanceOnItemCopy": true

This can happen for a few reasons, most commonly when the user<br>does not have (co-)admin permissions, or the application tries to create a<br>template with the `global` scope.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-recent-items">Recent items</h1>

Recent items represent items such
as files or folders that
the user accessed recently.

## List recently accessed items

<a id="opIdget_recent_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/recent_items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /recent_items`

Returns information about the recent items accessed
by a user, either in the last 90 days or up to the last
1000 items accessed.

This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|

|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-retention-policies">Retention policies</h1>

A retention policy blocks permanent deletion of content
for a specified amount of time. Admins can create
retention policies and then assign them to
specific folders or their entire enterprise.

## List retention policies

<a id="opIdget_retention_policies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/retention_policies \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /retention_policies`

Retrieves all of the retention policies for an enterprise.

<h3 id="list-retention-policies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|policy_name|query|string|false|Filters results by a case sensitive prefix of the name of<br>retention policies.|
|policy_type|query|string|false|Filters results by the type of retention policy.|
|created_by_user_id|query|string|false|Filters results by the ID of the user who created policy.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.|

## Create retention policy

<a id="opIdpost_retention_policies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/retention_policies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "policy_name": "Some Policy Name",
    "description": "Policy to retain all reports for at least one month",
    "policy_type": "finite",
    "disposition_action": "permanently_delete",
    "retention_length": "365",
    "retention_type": "modifiable",
    "can_owner_extend_retention": true,
    "max_extension_length": "365",
    "are_owners_notified": true,
    "custom_notification_recipients": [
      {
        "id": "11446498",
        "type": "user",
        "name": "Aaron Levie",
        "login": "ceo@example.com"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /retention_policies`

Creates a retention policy.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "policy_name": "Some Policy Name",
  "description": "Policy to retain all reports for at least one month",
  "policy_type": "finite",
  "disposition_action": "permanently_delete",
  "retention_length": "365",
  "retention_type": "modifiable",
  "can_owner_extend_retention": true,
  "max_extension_length": "365",
  "are_owners_notified": true,
  "custom_notification_recipients": [
    {
      "id": "11446498",
      "type": "user",
      "name": "Aaron Levie",
      "login": "ceo@example.com"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-retention-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» policy_name|body|string|true|The name for the retention policy.|
|» description|body|string|false|The additional text description of the retention policy.|
|» policy_type|body|string|true|The type of the retention policy. A retention<br>policy type can either be `finite`, where a<br>specific amount of time to retain the content is known<br>upfront, or `indefinite`, where the amount of time<br>to retain the content is still unknown.|
|» disposition_action|body|string|true|The disposition action of the retention policy.<br>`permanently_delete` deletes the content<br>retained by the policy permanently.<br>`remove_retention` lifts retention policy<br>from the content, allowing it to be deleted<br>by users once the retention policy has expired.|
|» retention_length|body|string(int32) \| null \| number(int32)|false|The length of the retention policy. This value<br>specifies the duration in days that the retention<br>policy will be active for after being assigned to<br>content.  If the policy has a `policy_type` of<br>`indefinite`, the `retention_length` will also be<br>`indefinite`.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string(int32) \| null|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|number(int32)|false|none|
|» retention_type|body|string|false|Specifies the retention type:<br><br>* `modifiable`: You can modify the retention policy. For example,<br>you can add or remove folders, shorten or lengthen<br>the policy duration, or delete the assignment.<br>Use this type if your retention policy<br>is not related to any regulatory purposes.<br><br>* `non_modifiable`: You can modify the retention policy<br>only in a limited way: add a folder, lengthen the duration,<br>retire the policy, change the disposition action<br>or notification settings. You cannot perform other actions,<br>such as deleting the assignment or shortening the<br>policy duration. Use this type to ensure<br>compliance with regulatory retention policies.|
|» can_owner_extend_retention|body|boolean|false|Whether the owner of a file will be allowed to<br>extend the retention.|
|» max_extension_length|body|[RetentionPolicyMaxExtensionLengthRequest](#schemaretentionpolicymaxextensionlengthrequest)|false|The maximum extension length of the retention date.<br>This value specifies the duration in days for which<br>the retention date of the file under policy can be extended.<br>It can be specified only for the 'finite' policy type<br>where the disposition action is 'permanently delete',<br>otherwise the server will return status 400.<br>If this value is 'none', it won't be possible to extend<br>the retention.|
|» are_owners_notified|body|boolean|false|Whether owner and co-owners of a file are notified<br>when the policy nears expiration.|
|» custom_notification_recipients|body|[[User--Mini](#schemauser--mini)]|false|A list of users notified when<br>the retention policy duration is about to end.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» policy_type|finite|
|» policy_type|indefinite|
|» disposition_action|permanently_delete|
|» disposition_action|remove_retention|
|» retention_type|modifiable|
|» retention_type|non_modifiable|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-retention-policy-assignments">Retention policy assignments</h1>

A Retention Policy Assignment is a relation
between a policy and folder or enterprise.
Creating an assignment puts a retention on
all the file versions that belong to that folder or enterprise.

## List retention policy assignments

<a id="opIdget_retention_policies_id_assignments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/retention_policies/982312/assignments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /retention_policies/{retention_policy_id}/assignments`

Returns a list of all retention policy assignments associated with a specified
retention policy.

<h3 id="list-retention-policy-assignments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|retention_policy_id|path|string|true|The ID of the retention policy.|
|type|query|string|false|The type of the retention policy assignment to retrieve.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

## Assign retention policy

<a id="opIdpost_retention_policy_assignments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/retention_policy_assignments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "policy_id": "173463",
    "assign_to": {
      "type": "metadata_template",
      "id": "6564564"
    },
    "filter_fields": [
      {
        "field": "a0f4ee4e-1dc1-4h90-a8a9-aef55fc681d4",
        "value": "0c27b756-0p87-4fe0-a43a-59fb661ccc4e"
      }
    ],
    "start_date_field": "upload_date"
  }'
```

`POST /retention_policy_assignments`

Assigns a retention policy to an item.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "policy_id": "173463",
  "assign_to": {
    "type": "metadata_template",
    "id": "6564564"
  },
  "filter_fields": [
    {
      "field": "a0f4ee4e-1dc1-4h90-a8a9-aef55fc681d4",
      "value": "0c27b756-0p87-4fe0-a43a-59fb661ccc4e"
    }
  ],
  "start_date_field": "upload_date"
}
```

<h3 id="assign-retention-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» policy_id|body|string|true|The ID of the retention policy to assign.|
|» assign_to|body|object|true|The item to assign the policy to.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of item to assign the policy to.|
|» » id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of item to assign the policy to.<br>Set to `null` or omit when `type` is set to<br>`enterprise`.|
|» filter_fields|body|[object]|false|If the `assign_to` type is `metadata_template`,<br>then optionally add the `filter_fields` parameter which will<br>require an array of objects with a field entry and a value entry.<br>Currently only one object of `field` and `value` is supported.|
|» » field|body|string|false|The metadata attribute key id.|
|» » value|body|string|false|The metadata attribute field id. For value, only<br>enum and multiselect types are supported.|
|» start_date_field|body|string|false|The date the retention policy assignment begins.<br><br>If the `assigned_to` type is `metadata_template`,<br>this field can be a date field's metadata attribute key id.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|enterprise|
|» » type|folder|
|» » type|metadata_template|

|404|Not Found|Returns an error if no retention policy with the given `policy_id` exists.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|Returns an error if a retention policy of equal or greater length has<br>already been assigned to this item.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
