<h1 id="box-platform-api-search">Search</h1>

The Box API provides a way to find content in Box
using full-text search queries.

## Query files/folders by metadata

<a id="opIdpost_metadata_queries_execute_read"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/metadata_queries/execute_read \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "from": "enterprise_123456.someTemplate",
    "query": "value >= :amount",
    "query_params": {
      "amount": "100"
    },
    "ancestor_folder_id": "0",
    "order_by": [
      {
        "field_key": "amount",
        "direction": "asc"
      }
    ],
    "limit": 50,
    "marker": "AAAAAmVYB1FWec8GH6yWu2nwmanfMh07IyYInaa7DZDYjgO1H4KoLW29vPlLY173OKsci6h6xGh61gG73gnaxoS+o0BbI1/h6le6cikjlupVhASwJ2Cj0tOD9wlnrUMHHw3/ISf+uuACzrOMhN6d5fYrbidPzS6MdhJOejuYlvsg4tcBYzjauP3+VU51p77HFAIuObnJT0ff",
    "fields": [
      "extension",
      "created_at",
      "item_status",
      "metadata.enterprise_1234.contracts",
      "metadata.enterprise_1234.regions.location"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /metadata_queries/execute_read`

For new integrations, use the [v2026.0 Query API](https://developer.box.com/reference/v2026.0/query-resources).
This is the latest version of the Query API, with advanced capabilities including multi-template queries and
Query Insights, and is the API we will continue to enhance with new Query capabilities.

Create a search using SQL-like syntax to return items that match specific
metadata.

By default, this endpoint returns only the most basic info about the items for
which the query matches. To get additional fields for each item, including any
of the metadata, use the `fields` attribute in the query.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "from": "enterprise_123456.someTemplate",
  "query": "value >= :amount",
  "query_params": {
    "amount": "100"
  },
  "ancestor_folder_id": "0",
  "order_by": [
    {
      "field_key": "amount",
      "direction": "asc"
    }
  ],
  "limit": 50,
  "marker": "AAAAAmVYB1FWec8GH6yWu2nwmanfMh07IyYInaa7DZDYjgO1H4KoLW29vPlLY173OKsci6h6xGh61gG73gnaxoS+o0BbI1/h6le6cikjlupVhASwJ2Cj0tOD9wlnrUMHHw3/ISf+uuACzrOMhN6d5fYrbidPzS6MdhJOejuYlvsg4tcBYzjauP3+VU51p77HFAIuObnJT0ff",
  "fields": [
    "extension",
    "created_at",
    "item_status",
    "metadata.enterprise_1234.contracts",
    "metadata.enterprise_1234.regions.location"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="query-filesfolders-by-metadata-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[MetadataQuery](#schemametadataquery)|false|none|
|» from|body|string|true|Specifies the template used in the query. Must be in the form<br>`scope.templateKey`. Not all templates can be used in this field,<br>most notably the built-in, Box-provided classification templates<br>can not be used in a query.|
|» query|body|string|false|The query to perform. A query is a logical expression that is very similar<br>to a SQL `SELECT` statement. Values in the search query can be turned into<br>parameters specified in the `query_param` arguments list to prevent having<br>to manually insert search values into the query string.<br><br>For example, a value of `:amount` would represent the `amount` value in<br>`query_params` object.|
|» query_params|body|object|false|Set of arguments corresponding to the parameters specified in the<br>`query`. The type of each parameter used in the `query_params` must match<br>the type of the corresponding metadata template field.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» ancestor_folder_id|body|string|true|The ID of the folder that you are restricting the query to. A<br>value of zero will return results from all folders you have access<br>to. A non-zero value will only return results found in the folder<br>corresponding to the ID or in any of its subfolders.|
|» order_by|body|[object]|false|A list of template fields and directions to sort the metadata query<br>results by.<br><br>The ordering `direction` must be the same for each item in the array.|
|» » field_key|body|string|false|The metadata template field to order by.<br><br>The `field_key` represents the `key` value of a field from the<br>metadata template being searched for.|
|» » direction|body|string|false|The direction to order by, either ascending or descending.<br><br>The `ordering` direction must be the same for each item in the<br>array.|
|» limit|body|integer|false|A value between 0 and 100 that indicates the maximum number of results<br>to return for a single request. This only specifies a maximum<br>boundary and will not guarantee the minimum number of results<br>returned.|
|» marker|body|string|false|Marker to use for requesting the next page.|
|» fields|body|[string]|false|By default, this endpoint returns only the most basic info about the items for<br>which the query matches. This attribute can be used to specify a list of<br>additional attributes to return for any item, including its metadata.<br><br>This attribute takes a list of item fields, metadata template identifiers,<br>or metadata template field identifiers.<br><br>For example:<br><br>* `created_by` will add the details of the user who created the item to<br>the response.<br>* `metadata.<scope>.<templateKey>` will return the mini-representation<br>of the metadata instance identified by the `scope` and `templateKey`.<br>* `metadata.<scope>.<templateKey>.<field>` will return all the mini-representation<br>of the metadata instance identified by the `scope` and `templateKey` plus<br>the field specified by the `field` name. Multiple fields for the same<br>`scope` and `templateKey` can be defined.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » direction|ASC|
|» » direction|DESC|
|» » direction|asc|
|» » direction|desc|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a list of files and folders that match this metadata query.|[MetadataQueryResults](#schemametadataqueryresults)|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error when the request body is not valid.<br><br>* `invalid_query` - Any of the provided body parameters might be<br>incorrect. This can mean the `query` is incorrect, as well as some cases<br>where the `from` value does not represent a valid template.<br>* `unexpected_json_type` - An argument from the `query` string is not<br>present in `query_param`. For example, `query` of `name = :name` requires<br>the `query_param` to include a value for the `name` argument, for example<br>`{ "name": "Box, Inc" }`.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error when a metadata template with the given `scope` and<br>`templateKey` can not be found. The error response will include extra<br>details.<br><br>* `instance_not_found` - The template was not found. Please make sure<br>to use the full template scope including the enterprise ID, like<br>`enterprise_12345`.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

## Search for content

<a id="opIdget_search"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /search`

Searches for files, folders, web links, and shared files across the
users content or across the entire enterprise.

<h3 id="search-for-content-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|The string to search for. This query is matched against item names,<br>descriptions, text content of files, and various other fields of<br>the different item types.<br><br>This parameter supports a variety of operators to further refine<br>the results returns.<br><br>* `""` - by wrapping a query in double quotes only exact matches are<br>  returned by the API. Exact searches do not return search matches<br>  based on specific character sequences. Instead, they return<br>  matches based on phrases, that is, word sequences. For example:<br>  A search for `"Blue-Box"` may return search results including<br>  the sequence `"blue.box"`, `"Blue Box"`, and `"Blue-Box"`;<br>  any item containing the words `Blue` and `Box` consecutively, in<br>  the order specified.<br>* `AND` - returns items that contain both the search terms. For<br>  example, a search for `marketing AND BoxWorks` returns items<br>  that have both `marketing` and `BoxWorks` within its text in any order.<br>  It does not return a result that only has `BoxWorks` in its text.<br>* `OR` - returns items that contain either of the search terms. For<br>  example, a search for `marketing OR BoxWorks` returns a result that<br>  has either `marketing` or `BoxWorks` within its text. Using this<br>  operator is not necessary as we implicitly interpret multi-word<br>  queries as `OR` unless another supported boolean term is used.<br>* `NOT` - returns items that do not contain the search term provided.<br>  For example, a search for `marketing AND NOT BoxWorks` returns a result<br>  that has only `marketing` within its text. Results containing<br>  `BoxWorks` are omitted.<br><br>We do not support lower case (that is,<br>`and`, `or`, and `not`) or mixed case (that is, `And`, `Or`, and `Not`)<br>operators.<br><br>This field is required unless the `mdfilters` parameter is defined.|
|scope|query|string|false|Limits the search results to either the files that the user has<br>access to, or to files available to the entire enterprise.<br><br>The scope defaults to `user_content`, which limits the search<br>results to content that is available to the currently authenticated<br>user.<br><br>The `enterprise_content` can be requested by an admin through our<br>support channels. Once this scope has been enabled for a user, it<br>will allow that use to query for content across the entire<br>enterprise and not only the content that they have access to.|
|file_extensions|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any files that match any of the provided<br>file extensions. This list is a comma-separated list of file extensions<br>without the dots.|
|created_at_range|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any items created within<br>a given date range.<br><br>Date ranges are defined as comma separated RFC3339<br>timestamps.<br><br>If the start date is omitted (`,2014-05-17T13:35:01-07:00`)<br>anything created before the end date will be returned.<br><br>If the end date is omitted (`2014-05-15T13:35:01-07:00,`) the<br>current date will be used as the end date instead.|
|updated_at_range|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any items updated within<br>a given date range.<br><br>Date ranges are defined as comma separated RFC3339<br>timestamps.<br><br>If the start date is omitted (`,2014-05-17T13:35:01-07:00`)<br>anything updated before the end date will be returned.<br><br>If the end date is omitted (`2014-05-15T13:35:01-07:00,`) the<br>current date will be used as the end date instead.|
|size_range|query|[integer]|false|Limits the search results to any items with a size within<br>a given file size range. This applied to files and folders.<br><br>Size ranges are defined as comma separated list of a lower<br>and upper byte size limit (inclusive).<br><br>The upper and lower bound can be omitted to create open ranges.|
|owner_user_ids|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any items that are owned<br>by the given list of owners, defined as a list of comma separated<br>user IDs.<br><br>The items still need to be owned or shared with<br>the currently authenticated user for them to show up in the search<br>results. If the user does not have access to any files owned by any of<br>the users an empty result set will be returned.<br><br>To search across an entire enterprise, we recommend using the<br>`enterprise_content` scope parameter which can be requested with our<br>support team.|
|recent_updater_user_ids|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any items that have been updated<br>by the given list of users, defined as a list of comma separated<br>user IDs.<br><br>The items still need to be owned or shared with<br>the currently authenticated user for them to show up in the search<br>results. If the user does not have access to any files owned by any of<br>the users an empty result set will be returned.<br><br>This feature only searches back to the last 10 versions of an item.|
|ancestor_folder_ids|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to items within the given<br>list of folders, defined as a comma separated lists<br>of folder IDs.<br><br>Search results will also include items within any subfolders<br>of those ancestor folders.<br><br>The folders still need to be owned or shared with<br>the currently authenticated user. If the folder is not accessible by this<br>user, or it does not exist, a `HTTP 404` error code will be returned<br>instead.<br><br>To search across an entire enterprise, we recommend using the<br>`enterprise_content` scope parameter which can be requested with our<br>support team.|
|content_types|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any items that match the search query<br>for a specific part of the file, for example the file description.<br><br>Content types are defined as a comma separated lists<br>of Box recognized content types. The allowed content types are as follows.<br><br>* `name` - The name of the item, as defined by its `name` field.<br>* `description` - The description of the item, as defined by its<br>  `description` field.<br>* `file_content` - The actual content of the file.<br>* `comments` - The content of any of the comments on a file or<br>   folder.<br>* `tags` - Any tags that are applied to an item, as defined by its<br>   `tags` field.|
|type|query|string|false|Limits the search results to any items of this type. This<br>parameter only takes one value. By default the API returns<br>items that match any of these types.<br><br>* `file` - Limits the search results to files,<br>* `folder` - Limits the search results to folders,<br>* `web_link` - Limits the search results to web links, also known<br>   as bookmarks.|
|trash_content|query|string|false|Determines if the search should look in the trash for items.<br><br>By default, this API only returns search results for items<br>not currently in the trash (`non_trashed_only`).<br><br>* `trashed_only` - Only searches for items currently in the trash<br>* `non_trashed_only` - Only searches for items currently not in<br>  the trash<br>* `all_items` - Searches for both trashed and non-trashed items.|
|mdfilters|query|[[MetadataFilter](#schemametadatafilter)]|false|Limits the search results to any items for which the metadata matches the provided filter.<br>This parameter is a list that specifies exactly **one** metadata template used to filter the search results.<br>The parameter is required unless the `query` parameter is provided.|
|sort|query|string|false|Defines the order in which search results are returned. This API<br>defaults to returning items by relevance unless this parameter is<br>explicitly specified.<br><br>* `relevance` (default) returns the results sorted by relevance to the<br>query search term. The relevance is based on the occurrence of the search<br>term in the items name, description, content, and additional properties.<br>* `modified_at` returns the results ordered in descending order by date<br>at which the item was last modified.|
|direction|query|string|false|Defines the direction in which search results are ordered. This API<br>defaults to returning items in descending (`DESC`) order unless this<br>parameter is explicitly specified.<br><br>When results are sorted by `relevance` the ordering is locked to returning<br>items in descending order of relevance, and this parameter is ignored.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Defines the maximum number of items to return as part of a page of<br>results.|
|include_recent_shared_links|query|boolean|false|Defines whether the search results should include any items<br>that the user recently accessed through a shared link.<br><br>When this parameter has been set to true,<br>the format of the response of this API changes to return<br>a list of [Search Results with<br>Shared Links](https://developer.box.com/reference/resources/search-results-with-shared-links).|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|
|deleted_user_ids|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to items that were deleted by the given<br>list of users, defined as a list of comma separated user IDs.<br><br>The `trash_content` parameter needs to be set to `trashed_only`.<br><br>If searching in trash is not performed, an empty result set<br>is returned. The items need to be owned or shared with<br>the currently authenticated user for them to show up in the search<br>results.<br><br>If the user does not have access to any files owned by<br>any of the users, an empty result set is returned.<br><br>Data available from 2023-02-01 onwards.|
|deleted_at_range|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any items deleted within a given<br>date range.<br><br>Date ranges are defined as comma separated RFC3339 timestamps.<br><br>If the start date is omitted (`2014-05-17T13:35:01-07:00`),<br>anything deleted before the end date will be returned.<br><br>If the end date is omitted (`2014-05-15T13:35:01-07:00`),<br>the current date will be used as the end date instead.<br><br>The `trash_content` parameter needs to be set to `trashed_only`.<br><br>If searching in trash is not performed, then an empty result<br>is returned.<br><br>Data available from 2023-02-01 onwards.|

|400|Bad Request|Returns an error when the request was not valid. This can have multiple<br>reasons and the `context_info` object will provide you with more details.<br><br>* `missing_parameter` - Please provide at least the `query` or `mdfilters`<br>  query parameter in a search.<br>* `invalid_parameter` - Any of the fields might not be in the right<br>  format. This could for example mean that one of the RFC3339 dates is<br>  incorrect, or a string is provided where an integer is expected.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns an error when the user does not have the permission to make<br>this API call.<br><br>* The developer provided a `scope` of `enterprise_content` but did<br>  not request this scope to be enabled for the user through our<br>  support channels.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error when the user does not have access to an item<br>mentioned in the request.<br><br>* The developer provided a folder ID in `ancestor_folder_ids`<br>  that either does not exist or the user does not have access to.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-session-termination">Session termination</h1>

Session termination API is used to
validate the roles and permissions of the group,
and creates asynchronous jobs to terminate the group's sessions.

## Create jobs to terminate users session

<a id="opIdpost_users_terminate_sessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/users/terminate_sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_ids": [
      "123456",
      "456789"
    ],
    "user_logins": [
      "user@sample.com",
      "user2@sample.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /users/terminate_sessions`

Validates the roles and permissions of the user,
and creates asynchronous jobs
to terminate the user's sessions.
Returns the status for the POST request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_ids": [
    "123456",
    "456789"
  ],
  "user_logins": [
    "user@sample.com",
    "user2@sample.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-jobs-to-terminate-users-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» user_ids|body|[string]|true|A list of user IDs.|
|» user_logins|body|[string]|true|A list of user logins.|

## Create jobs to terminate user group session

<a id="opIdpost_groups_terminate_sessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/groups/terminate_sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "group_ids": [
      "123456",
      "456789"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /groups/terminate_sessions`

Validates the roles and permissions of the group,
and creates asynchronous jobs
to terminate the group's sessions.
Returns the status for the POST request.

> Body parameter

{
  "group_ids": [
    "123456",
    "456789"
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-shared-links-files">Shared links (Files)</h1>

Files shared links are URLs that are generated for files stored in Box,
which provide direct, read-only access to the resource.

## Find file for shared link

<a id="opIdget_shared_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/shared_items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'boxapi: shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]'
```

`GET /shared_items`

Returns the file represented by a shared link.

A shared file can be represented by a shared link,
which can originate within the current enterprise or within another.

This endpoint allows an application to retrieve information about a
shared file when only given a shared link.

The `shared_link_permission_options` array field can be returned
by requesting it in the `fields` query parameter.

<h3 id="find-file-for-shared-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|if-none-match|header|string|false|Ensures an item is only returned if it has changed.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `304 Not Modified` if the item has not<br>changed since.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|boxapi|header|string|true|A header containing the shared link and optional password for the<br>shared link.<br><br>The format for this header is as follows:<br><br>`shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`.|

## Get shared link for file

<a id="opIdget_files_id#get_shared_link"></a>

curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345#get_shared_link?fields=shared_link' \

```

`GET /files/{file_id}#get_shared_link`

## Add shared link to file

<a id="opIdput_files_id#add_shared_link"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345#add_shared_link?fields=shared_link' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "permissions": {
        "can_download": true,
        "can_preview": true,
        "can_edit": true
      },
      "one_time_passcode": {
        "mode": "none"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /files/{file_id}#add_shared_link`

Adds a shared link to a file.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true,
      "can_preview": true,
      "can_edit": true
    },
    "one_time_passcode": {
      "mode": "none"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-shared-link-to-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|string|true|Explicitly request the `shared_link` fields<br>to be returned for this item.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|The settings for the shared link to create on the file.<br>Use an empty object (`{}`) to use the default settings for shared<br>links.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the file (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string \| null|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br>Passwords must now be at least eight characters<br>long and include a number, upper case letter, or<br>a non-numeric or non-alphabetic character.<br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared<br>links.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts. The value must be greater than the<br>current date and time.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » » can_preview|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for previewing of files.<br>This value is always `true`. For shared links on folders<br>this also applies to any items in the folder.|
|» » » can_edit|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for editing of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.<br>This value can only be `true` is `can_download` is<br>also `true`.|
|» » one_time_passcode|body|object|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableNone](#schemasharedlinkotpwritablenone)|false|One-time-passcode (OTP) enforcement is turned off. The shared link is<br>accessible without any one-time-passcode verification.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableOpen](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableopen)|false|Any anonymous recipient can request a one-time-passcode to any email<br>address and access the shared link after verifying it. Collaborators<br>and registered Box users access the link without being prompted.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableAllowlist](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableallowlist)|false|Anonymous recipients can request a one-time-passcode only when they<br>enter an email that matches an entry on the `allowlist`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|

## Update shared link on file

<a id="opIdput_files_id#update_shared_link"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345#update_shared_link?fields=shared_link' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "permissions": {
        "can_download": true,
        "can_preview": true,
        "can_edit": true
      },
      "one_time_passcode": {
        "mode": "none"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /files/{file_id}#update_shared_link`

Updates a shared link on a file.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true,
      "can_preview": true,
      "can_edit": true
    },
    "one_time_passcode": {
      "mode": "none"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-shared-link-on-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|string|true|Explicitly request the `shared_link` fields<br>to be returned for this item.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|The settings for the shared link to update.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string \| null|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br>Passwords must now be at least eight characters<br>long and include a number, upper case letter, or<br>a non-numeric or non-alphabetic character.<br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared<br>links.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts. The value must be greater than the<br>current date and time.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » » can_preview|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for previewing of files.<br>This value is always `true`. For shared links on folders<br>this also applies to any items in the folder.|
|» » » can_edit|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for editing of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.<br>This value can only be `true` is `can_download` is<br>also `true`.|
|» » one_time_passcode|body|object|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableNone](#schemasharedlinkotpwritablenone)|false|One-time-passcode (OTP) enforcement is turned off. The shared link is<br>accessible without any one-time-passcode verification.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableOpen](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableopen)|false|Any anonymous recipient can request a one-time-passcode to any email<br>address and access the shared link after verifying it. Collaborators<br>and registered Box users access the link without being prompted.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableAllowlist](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableallowlist)|false|Anonymous recipients can request a one-time-passcode only when they<br>enter an email that matches an entry on the `allowlist`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-shared-links-folders">Shared links (Folders)</h1>

Folders shared links are URLs that are generated for folders stored in Box,
which provide direct, read-only access to the resource.

## Find folder for shared link

<a id="opIdget_shared_items#folders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/shared_items#folders' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'boxapi: shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]'
```

`GET /shared_items#folders`

Return the folder represented by a shared link.

A shared folder can be represented by a shared link,
which can originate within the current enterprise or within another.

This endpoint allows an application to retrieve information about a
shared folder when only given a shared link.

<h3 id="find-folder-for-shared-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|if-none-match|header|string|false|Ensures an item is only returned if it has changed.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `304 Not Modified` if the item has not<br>changed since.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|boxapi|header|string|true|A header containing the shared link and optional password for the<br>shared link.<br><br>The format for this header is as follows:<br><br>`shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`.|

## Get shared link for folder

<a id="opIdget_folders_id#get_shared_link"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/12345#get_shared_link?fields=shared_link' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /folders/{folder_id}#get_shared_link`

Gets the information for a shared link on a folder.

<h3 id="get-shared-link-for-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|string|true|Explicitly request the `shared_link` fields<br>to be returned for this item.|

## Add shared link to folder

<a id="opIdput_folders_id#add_shared_link"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/12345#add_shared_link?fields=shared_link' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "permissions": {
        "can_download": true,
        "can_preview": true,
        "can_edit": false
      },
      "one_time_passcode": {
        "mode": "none"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /folders/{folder_id}#add_shared_link`

Adds a shared link to a folder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true,
      "can_preview": true,
      "can_edit": false
    },
    "one_time_passcode": {
      "mode": "none"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-shared-link-to-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|string|true|Explicitly request the `shared_link` fields<br>to be returned for this item.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|The settings for the shared link to create on the folder.<br><br>Use an empty object (`{}`) to use the default settings for shared<br>links.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string \| null|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br>Passwords must now be at least eight characters<br>long and include a number, upper case letter, or<br>a non-numeric or non-alphabetic character.<br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared<br>links.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts. The value must be greater than the<br>current date and time.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » » can_preview|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for previewing of files.<br>This value is always `true`. For shared links on folders<br>this also applies to any items in the folder.|
|» » » can_edit|body|boolean|false|This value can only be `false` for items<br>with a `type` of `folder`.|
|» » one_time_passcode|body|object|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableNone](#schemasharedlinkotpwritablenone)|false|One-time-passcode (OTP) enforcement is turned off. The shared link is<br>accessible without any one-time-passcode verification.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableOpen](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableopen)|false|Any anonymous recipient can request a one-time-passcode to any email<br>address and access the shared link after verifying it. Collaborators<br>and registered Box users access the link without being prompted.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableAllowlist](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableallowlist)|false|Anonymous recipients can request a one-time-passcode only when they<br>enter an email that matches an entry on the `allowlist`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|

|---|---|---|---|

|412|Precondition Failed|Returns an error when the `If-Match` header does not match<br>the current `etag` value of the folder. This indicates that the folder<br>has changed since it was last requested.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

## Update shared link on folder

<a id="opIdput_folders_id#update_shared_link"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/12345#update_shared_link?fields=shared_link' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",

      "permissions": {
        "can_download": true,
        "can_preview": true,
        "can_edit": false
      },

      }

`PUT /folders/{folder_id}#update_shared_link`

Updates a shared link on a folder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true,
      "can_preview": true,
      "can_edit": false
    },
    "one_time_passcode": {
      "mode": "none"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-shared-link-on-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|string|true|Explicitly request the `shared_link` fields<br>to be returned for this item.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|The settings for the shared link to update.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br>Passwords must now be at least eight characters<br>long and include a number, upper case letter, or<br>a non-numeric or non-alphabetic character.<br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared<br>links.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts. The value must be greater than the<br>current date and time.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » » can_preview|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for previewing of files.<br>This value is always `true`. For shared links on folders<br>this also applies to any items in the folder.|
|» » » can_edit|body|boolean|false|This value can only be `false` for items<br>with a `type` of `folder`.|
|» » one_time_passcode|body|object|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableNone](#schemasharedlinkotpwritablenone)|false|One-time-passcode (OTP) enforcement is turned off. The shared link is<br>accessible without any one-time-passcode verification.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableOpen](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableopen)|false|Any anonymous recipient can request a one-time-passcode to any email<br>address and access the shared link after verifying it. Collaborators<br>and registered Box users access the link without being prompted.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableAllowlist](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableallowlist)|false|Anonymous recipients can request a one-time-passcode only when they<br>enter an email that matches an entry on the `allowlist`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-shared-links-web-links">Shared links (Web Links)</h1>

Web links for files are URLs that are generated
for web links in Box,
which provide direct, read-only access to the resource.

## Find web link for shared link

<a id="opIdget_shared_items#web_links"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/shared_items#web_links' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'boxapi: shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]'
```

`GET /shared_items#web_links`

Returns the web link represented by a shared link.

A shared web link can be represented by a shared link,
which can originate within the current enterprise or within another.

This endpoint allows an application to retrieve information about a
shared web link when only given a shared link.

<h3 id="find-web-link-for-shared-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|if-none-match|header|string|false|Ensures an item is only returned if it has changed.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `304 Not Modified` if the item has not<br>changed since.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|boxapi|header|string|true|A header containing the shared link and optional password for the<br>shared link.<br><br>The format for this header is as follows:<br><br>`shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`.|

## Add shared link to web link

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/web_links/12345#add_shared_link?fields=shared_link' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "permissions": {
        "can_download": true,
        "can_preview": true,
        "can_edit": false
      },
      "one_time_passcode": {
        "mode": "none"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /web_links/{web_link_id}#add_shared_link`

Adds a shared link to a web link.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-n8t-use-this-Password",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true,
      "can_preview": true,
      "can_edit": false
    },
    "one_time_passcode": {
      "mode": "none"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-shared-link-to-web-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|web_link_id|path|string|true|The ID of the web link.|
|fields|query|string|true|Explicitly request the `shared_link` fields<br>to be returned for this item.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|The settings for the shared link to create on the web link.<br><br>Use an empty object (`{}`) to use the default settings for shared<br>links.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the file (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string \| null|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br>Passwords must now be at least eight characters<br>long and include a number, upper case letter, or<br>a non-numeric or non-alphabetic character.<br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared<br>links.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts. The value must be greater than the<br>current date and time.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » » can_preview|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for previewing of files.<br>This value is always `true`. For shared links on folders<br>this also applies to any items in the folder.|
|» » » can_edit|body|boolean|false|This value can only be `true` is `type` is `file`.|
|» » one_time_passcode|body|object|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableNone](#schemasharedlinkotpwritablenone)|false|One-time-passcode (OTP) enforcement is turned off. The shared link is<br>accessible without any one-time-passcode verification.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableOpen](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableopen)|false|Any anonymous recipient can request a one-time-passcode to any email<br>address and access the shared link after verifying it. Collaborators<br>and registered Box users access the link without being prompted.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableAllowlist](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableallowlist)|false|Anonymous recipients can request a one-time-passcode only when they<br>enter an email that matches an entry on the `allowlist`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-shared-links-app-items">Shared links (App Items)</h1>

URLs generated for app items stored in Box,
which provide direct, read-only access to the resource.

## Find app item for shared link

<a id="opIdget_shared_items#app_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/shared_items#app_items' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'boxapi: shared_link=[example.com]&shared_link_password=[xyz123]'
```

`GET /shared_items#app_items`

Returns the app item represented by a shared link.

The link can originate from the current enterprise or another.

<h3 id="find-app-item-for-shared-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boxapi|header|string|true|A header containing the shared link and optional password for the<br>shared link.<br><br>The format for this header is `shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{

<h1 id="box-platform-api-shield-information-barriers">Shield information barriers</h1>

Shield information barrier in Box defines an ethical wall.
An ethical wall is a mechanism that prevents exchanges or communication that
could lead to conflicts of interest and therefore result in
business activities ethically or legally questionable.

<h1 id="box-platform-api-shield-information-barrier-segments">Shield information barrier segments</h1>

<h1 id="box-platform-api-box-sign-templates">Box Sign templates</h1>

are automatically populated with data when creating the request.

<h1 id="box-platform-api-skills">Skills</h1>

Box Skills are designed to allow custom processing
of files uploaded to Box, with the
intent of enhancing the underlying metadata of the file.

## List Box Skill cards on file

<a id="opIdget_files_id_metadata_global_boxSkillsCards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345/metadata/global/boxSkillsCards \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /files/{file_id}/metadata/global/boxSkillsCards`

## Update Box Skill cards on file

<a id="opIdput_files_id_metadata_global_boxSkillsCards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345/metadata/global/boxSkillsCards \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json-patch+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "op": "replace",
      "path": "/cards/0",
      "value": {
        "created_at": "2018-04-13T13:53:23-07:00",
        "type": "skill_card",
        "skill_card_type": "keyword",
        "skill_card_title": {
          "code": "labels",
          "message": "Labels"
        },
        "skill": {
          "type": "service",
          "id": "image-recognition-service"
        },
        "invocation": {
          "type": "skill_invocation",
          "id": "image-recognition-service-123"
        },
        "entries": [
          {
            "text": "keyword1"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]'
```

`PUT /files/{file_id}/metadata/global/boxSkillsCards`

Updates one or more Box Skills metadata cards to a file.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "op": "replace",
    "path": "/cards/0",
    "value": {
      "created_at": "2018-04-13T13:53:23-07:00",
      "type": "skill_card",
      "skill_card_type": "keyword",
      "skill_card_title": {
        "code": "labels",
        "message": "Labels"
      },
      "skill": {
        "type": "service",
        "id": "image-recognition-service"
      },
      "invocation": {
        "type": "skill_invocation",
        "id": "image-recognition-service-123"
      },
      "entries": [
        {
          "text": "keyword1"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
]
```

<h3 id="update-box-skill-cards-on-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|body|body|[object]|false|none|
|» op|body|string|false|The value will always be `replace`.|
|» path|body|string|false|The JSON Path that represents the card to replace. In most cases<br>this will be in the format `/cards/{index}` where `index` is the<br>zero-indexed position of the card in the list of cards.|
|» value|body|object|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[KeywordSkillCard](#schemakeywordskillcard)|false|A skill card that contains a set of keywords.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[TimelineSkillCard](#schematimelineskillcard)|false|A Box Skill metadata card that places a list of images on a<br>timeline.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[TranscriptSkillCard](#schematranscriptskillcard)|false|A Box Skill metadata card that adds a transcript to a file.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[StatusSkillCard](#schemastatusskillcard)|false|A Box Skill metadata card that puts a status message in the metadata sidebar.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» op|replace|

`PUT /skill_invocations/{skill_id}`

An alternative method that can be used to overwrite and update all Box Skill
metadata cards on a file.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "metadata": {
    "cards": [
      {
        "created_at": "2018-04-13T13:53:23-07:00",
        "type": "skill_card",
        "skill_card_type": "keyword",
        "skill_card_title": {
          "code": "labels",
          "message": "Labels"
        },
        "skill": {
          "type": "service",
          "id": "image-recognition-service"
        },
        "invocation": {
          "type": "skill_invocation",
          "id": "image-recognition-service-123"
        },
        "entries": [
          {
            "text": "keyword1"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "file": {
    "type": "file",
    "id": "3243244"
  },
  "file_version": {
    "type": "file_version",
    "id": "731381601045"
  },
  "usage": {
    "unit": "file",
    "value": 1
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-all-box-skill-cards-on-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|skill_id|path|string|true|The ID of the skill to apply this metadata for.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» status|body|string|true|Defines the status of this invocation. Set this to `success` when setting Skill cards.|
|» metadata|body|object|true|The metadata to set for this skill. This is a list of<br>Box Skills cards. These cards will overwrite any existing Box<br>skill cards on the file.|
|» » cards|body|[[SkillCard](#schemaskillcard)]|false|A list of Box Skill cards to apply to this file.|
|» file|body|object|true|The file to assign the cards to.|
|» » type|body|string|false|The value will always be `file`.|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of the file.|
|» file_version|body|object|false|The optional file version to assign the cards to.|
|» » type|body|string|false|The value will always be `file_version`.|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of the file version.|
|» usage|body|object|false|A descriptor that defines what items are affected by this call.<br><br>Set this to the default values when setting a card to a `success`<br>state, and leave it out in most other situations.|
|» » unit|body|string|false|The value will always be `file`.|
|» » value|body|number|false|Number of resources affected.|

|» status|success|
|» status|transient_failure|
|» status|permanent_failure|
|» » type|file|
|» » type|file_version|

<a id="opIddelete_storage_policy_assignments_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /storage_policy_assignments/{storage_policy_assignment_id}`

Delete a storage policy assignment.

Deleting a storage policy assignment on a user
will have the user inherit the enterprise's default
storage policy.

There is a rate limit for calling this endpoint of only
twice per user in a 24 hour time frame.

<h3 id="unassign-storage-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|404|Not Found|Returns an error when the task could not be found or the user does not<br>have access to the file the task is assigned to.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Returns an error if the task assignment ID was omitted in<br>the request.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Assign task

<a id="opIdpost_task_assignments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/task_assignments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "task": {
      "id": "11446498",
      "type": "task"
    },
    "assign_to": {
      "id": "3242343",
      "login": "john@example.com"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /task_assignments`

Assigns a task to a user.

A task can be assigned to more than one user by creating multiple
assignments.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "task": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "task"
  },
  "assign_to": {
    "id": "3242343",
    "login": "john@example.com"
  }
}

|» assign_to|body|object|true|The user to assign the task to.|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of the user to assign to the<br>task.<br><br>To specify a user by their email<br>address use the `login` parameter.|

`PUT /task_assignments/{task_assignment_id}`

<h1 id="box-platform-api-tasks">Tasks</h1>

Tasks allow users to request collaborators on a file
to review a file or complete a piece of work.
Tasks can be used by developers to create file-centric workflows.

## Create task

<a id="opIdpost_tasks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/tasks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "item": {
      "id": "11446498",
      "type": "file"
    },
    "action": "review",
    "message": "Please review",
    "due_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "completion_rule": "all_assignees"
  }'
```

`POST /tasks`

Creates a single task on a file. This task is not assigned to any user and
will need to be assigned separately.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "item": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "file"
  },
  "action": "review",
  "message": "Please review",
  "due_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "completion_rule": "all_assignees"
}
```

<h3 id="create-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» item|body|object|true|The file to attach the task to.|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of the file.|
|» » type|body|string|false|The value will always be `file`.|
|» action|body|string|false|The action the task assignee will be prompted to do. Must be<br><br>* `review` defines an approval task that can be approved or,<br>rejected<br>* `complete` defines a general task which can be completed.|
|» message|body|string|false|An optional message to include with the task.|
|» due_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Defines when the task is due. Defaults to `null` if not<br>provided.|
|» completion_rule|body|string|false|Defines which assignees need to complete this task before the task<br>is considered completed.<br><br>* `all_assignees` (default) requires all assignees to review or<br>approve the task in order for it to be considered completed.<br>* `any_assignee` accepts any one assignee to review or<br>approve the task in order for it to be considered completed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|file|
|» action|review|
|» action|complete|
|» completion_rule|all_assignees|
|» completion_rule|any_assignee|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "11446498",
  "type": "task",
  "item": {
    "id": "12345",
    "etag": "1",
    "type": "file",
    "sequence_id": {},
    "name": "Contract.pdf",
    "sha1": "85136C79CBF9FE36BB9D05D0639C70C265C18D37",
    "file_version": {
      "id": "12345",
      "type": "file_version",
      "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc"
    }
  },
  "due_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "action": "review",
  "message": "Legal review",
  "task_assignment_collection": {
    "total_count": 100,

## Update task

<a id="opIdput_tasks_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/tasks/12345 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "action": "review",
    "message": "Please review",
    "due_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "completion_rule": "all_assignees"
  }'
```

`PUT /tasks/{task_id}`

Updates a task. This can be used to update a task's configuration, or to
update its completion state.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action": "review",
  "message": "Please review",
  "due_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "completion_rule": "all_assignees"
}
```

<h3 id="update-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_id|path|string|true|The ID of the task.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» action|body|string|false|The action the task assignee will be prompted to do. Must be<br><br>* `review` defines an approval task that can be approved or<br>rejected,<br>* `complete` defines a general task which can be completed.|
|» message|body|string|false|The message included with the task.|
|» due_at|body|string(date-time)|false|When the task is due at.|
|» completion_rule|body|string|false|Defines which assignees need to complete this task before the task<br>is considered completed.<br><br>* `all_assignees` (default) requires all assignees to review or<br>approve the task in order for it to be considered completed.<br>* `any_assignee` accepts any one assignee to review or<br>approve the task in order for it to be considered completed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|review|
|» action|complete|
|» completion_rule|all_assignees|
|» completion_rule|any_assignee|

> Example responses

<h1 id="box-platform-api-terms-of-service-user-statuses">Terms of service user statuses</h1>

manage the status of terms of service
for a particular user.

<h1 id="box-platform-api-transfer-folders">Transfer folders</h1>

API designed to move all of the items
(files, folders and workflows)
owned by a user into another user's account.

## Transfer owned folders

<a id="opIdput_users_id_folders_0"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/users/12345/folders/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "owned_by": {
      "id": "1232234"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /users/{user_id}/folders/0`

Move all of the items (files, folders and workflows) owned by a user into
another user's account.

Only the root folder (`0`) can be transferred.

Folders can only be moved across users by users with administrative
permissions.

All existing shared links and folder-level collaborations are transferred
during the operation. Please note that while collaborations at the individual
file-level are transferred during the operation, the collaborations are
deleted when the original user is deleted.

If the user has a large number of items across all folders, the call will
be run asynchronously. If the operation is not completed within 10 minutes,
the user will receive a 200 OK response, and the operation will continue running.

If the destination path has a metadata cascade policy attached to any of
the parent folders, a metadata cascade operation will be kicked off
asynchronously.

There is currently no way to check for when this operation is finished.

The destination folder's name will be in the format `{User}'s Files and
Folders`, where `{User}` is the display name of the user.

To make this API call your application will need to have the "Read and write
all files and folders stored in Box" scope enabled.

Please make sure the destination user has access to `Relay` or `Relay Lite`,
and has access to the files and folders involved in the workflows being
transferred.

Admins will receive an email when the operation is completed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "owned_by": {
    "id": "1232234"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="transfer-owned-folders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|notify|query|boolean|false|Determines if users should receive email notification<br>for the action performed.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» owned_by|body|object|true|The user who the folder will be transferred to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the user who the folder will be<br>transferred to.|

## Restore file

<a id="opIdpost_files_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345 \
  -X POST \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Restored.docx",
    "parent": {
      "id": "123"
    }
  }'

`POST /files/{file_id}`

Restores a file that has been moved to the trash.

An optional new parent ID can be provided to restore the file to in case the
original folder has been deleted.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Restored.docx",
  "parent": {
    "id": "123"
  }
}

This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|

## Get trashed file

<a id="opIdget_files_id_trash"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345/trash \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /files/{file_id}/trash`

Retrieves a file that has been moved to the trash.

Please note that only if the file itself has been moved to the
trash can it be retrieved with this API call. If instead one of
its parent folders was moved to the trash, only that folder
can be inspected using the
[`GET /folders/:id/trash`](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-folders-id-trash) API.

To list all items that have been moved to the trash, please
use the [`GET /folders/trash/items`](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-folders-trash-items/)
API.

<h3 id="get-trashed-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-trashed-folders">Trashed folders</h1>

Folders that were deleted and
are in trash.

## Restore folder

<a id="opIdpost_folders_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/12345 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Restored Photos",
    "parent": {
      "id": "123"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /folders/{folder_id}`

Restores a folder that has been moved to the trash.

An optional new parent ID can be provided to restore the folder to in case the
original folder has been deleted.

During this operation, part of the file tree will be locked, mainly
the source folder and all of its descendants, as well as the destination
folder.

For the duration of the operation, no other move, copy, delete, or restore
operation can performed on any of the locked folders.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Restored Photos",
  "parent": {
    "id": "123"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="restore-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|An optional new name for the folder.|
|» parent|body|object|false|none|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of parent item.|

For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|

## Permanently remove folder

<a id="opIddelete_folders_id_trash"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/12345/trash \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /folders/{folder_id}/trash`

Permanently deletes a folder that is in the trash.
This action cannot be undone.

<h3 id="permanently-remove-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-trashed-items">Trashed items</h1>

Items that were deleted and
are in trash.

## List trashed items

<a id="opIdget_folders_trash_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/folders/trash/items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /folders/trash/items`

Retrieves the files and folders that have been moved
to the trash.

Any attribute in the full files or folders objects can be passed
in with the `fields` parameter to retrieve those specific
attributes that are not returned by default.

This endpoint defaults to use offset-based pagination, yet also supports
marker-based pagination using the `marker` parameter.  

The number of entries returned may be less than `total_count`. For example, if a user deletes items from a shared folder and is later removed as a collaborator, those deleted items will no longer appear in this endpoint’s results, even though they are still included in `total_count`.

<h3 id="list-trashed-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|
|usemarker|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether to use marker-based pagination instead of<br>offset-based pagination. Only one pagination method can<br>be used at a time.<br><br>By setting this value to true, the API will return a `marker` field<br>that can be passed as a parameter to this endpoint to get the next<br>page of the response.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort results in. This can be either in alphabetical ascending<br>(`ASC`) or descending (`DESC`) order.|
|sort|query|string|false|Defines the **second** attribute by which items<br>are sorted.<br><br>Items are always sorted by their `type` first, with<br>folders listed before files, and files listed<br>before web links.<br><br>This parameter is not supported when using marker-based pagination.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|ASC|
|direction|DESC|
|sort|name|
|sort|date|
|sort|size|
