<h1 id="box-platform-api-trashed-web-links">Trashed web links</h1>

Web links that were deleted and
are in trash.

## Restore web link

<a id="opIdpost_web_links_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/web_links/12345 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Restored.docx",
    "parent": {
      "id": "123"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /web_links/{web_link_id}`

Restores a web link that has been moved to the trash.

An optional new parent ID can be provided to restore the  web link to in case
the original folder has been deleted.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Restored.docx",
  "parent": {
    "id": "123"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="restore-web-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|web_link_id|path|string|true|The ID of the web link.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|An optional new name for the web link.|
|» parent|body|object|false|none|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of parent item.|


`GET /web_links/{web_link_id}/trash`

Retrieves a web link that has been moved to the trash.

<h3 id="get-trashed-web-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|web_link_id|path|string|true|The ID of the web link.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|

## Permanently remove web link

<a id="opIddelete_web_links_id_trash"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/web_links/12345/trash \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /web_links/{web_link_id}/trash`

Permanently deletes a web link that is in the trash.
This action cannot be undone.

<h3 id="permanently-remove-web-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|web_link_id|path|string|true|The ID of the web link.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-uploads">Uploads</h1>

The direct file upload API supports files
up to 50MB in size and sends all
the binary data to the Box API in 1 API request.

## Upload file version

<a id="opIdpost_files_id_content"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345/content \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'attributes={"name":"Photo 2.0.png","content_modified_at":"2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00"}' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /files/{file_id}/content`

Update a file's content. For file sizes over 50MB we recommend
using the Chunk Upload APIs.

The `attributes` part of the body must come **before** the
`file` part. Requests that do not follow this format when
uploading the file will receive a HTTP `400` error with a
`metadata_after_file_contents` error code.

> Body parameter

```yaml
attributes:
  name: Photo 2.0.png
  content_modified_at: "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00"
file: string
```

<h3 id="upload-file-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|content-md5|header|string|false|An optional header containing the SHA1 hash of the file to<br>ensure that the file was not corrupted in transit.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» attributes|body|object|true|The additional attributes of the file being uploaded. Mainly the<br>name and the parent folder. These attributes are part of the multi<br>part request body and are in JSON format.<br><br><Message warning><br><br>  The `attributes` part of the body must come **before** the<br>  `file` part. Requests that do not follow this format when<br>  uploading the file will receive a HTTP `400` error with a<br>  `metadata_after_file_contents` error code.<br><br></Message>|
|» » name|body|string|true|An optional new name for the file. If specified, the file<br>will be renamed when the new version is uploaded.|
|» » content_modified_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Defines the time the file was last modified at.<br><br>If not set, the upload time will be used.|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The content of the file to upload to Box.<br><br><Message warning><br><br>  The `attributes` part of the body must come **before** the<br>  `file` part. Requests that do not follow this format when<br>  uploading the file will receive a HTTP `400` error with a<br>  `metadata_after_file_contents` error code.<br><br></Message>|

## Upload file

<a id="opIdpost_files_content"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/content \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'attributes={"name":"Photo.png","parent":{"id":"124132"},"content_created_at":"2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00","content_modified_at":"2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00"}' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /files/content`

Uploads a small file to Box. For file sizes over 50MB we recommend
using the Chunk Upload APIs.

The `attributes` part of the body must come **before** the
`file` part. Requests that do not follow this format when
uploading the file will receive a HTTP `400` error with a
`metadata_after_file_contents` error code.

> Body parameter

```yaml
attributes:
  name: Photo.png
  parent:
    id: "124132"
  content_created_at: "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00"
  content_modified_at: "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00"
file: string
```

<h3 id="upload-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|content-md5|header|string|false|An optional header containing the SHA1 hash of the file to<br>ensure that the file was not corrupted in transit.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» attributes|body|object|true|The additional attributes of the file being uploaded. Mainly the<br>name and the parent folder. These attributes are part of the multi<br>part request body and are in JSON format.<br><br><Message warning><br><br>  The `attributes` part of the body must come **before** the<br>  `file` part. Requests that do not follow this format when<br>  uploading the file will receive a HTTP `400` error with a<br>  `metadata_after_file_contents` error code.<br><br></Message>|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the file.<br><br>File names must be unique within their parent folder. The name check is case-insensitive, so a file<br>named `New File` cannot be created in a parent folder that already contains a folder named `new file`.|
|» » parent|body|object|true|The parent folder to upload the file to.|
|» » » id|body|string|true|The id of the parent folder. Use<br>`0` for the user's root folder.|
|» » content_created_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Defines the time the file was originally created at.<br><br>If not set, the upload time will be used.|
|» » content_modified_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Defines the time the file was last modified at.<br><br>If not set, the upload time will be used.|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The content of the file to upload to Box.<br><br><Message warning><br><br>  The `attributes` part of the body must come **before** the<br>  `file` part. Requests that do not follow this format when<br>  uploading the file will receive a HTTP `400` error with a<br>  `metadata_after_file_contents` error code.<br><br></Message>|

|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if some of the parameters are missing or<br>not valid.<br>* `bad_request` when a parameter is missing or incorrect.<br>* `item_name_too_long` when the folder name is too long.<br>* `item_name_invalid` when the folder name contains<br>  non-valid characters.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error if the parent folder<br>does not exist or if the user<br>is not authorized to access the parent folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|Returns an error if the file already exists,<br>or the account has run out of disk space.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

<h1 id="box-platform-api-uploads-chunked">Uploads (Chunked)</h1>

The chunked upload endpoints support files from
20MB in size and allow an application
to upload the file in parts,
allowing for more control to catch any errors
and retry parts individually.

## Create upload session

<a id="opIdpost_files_upload_sessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/upload_sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "folder_id": "0",
    "file_size": 104857600,
    "file_name": "Project.mov"
  }'
```

`POST /files/upload_sessions`

Creates an upload session for a new file.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "folder_id": "0",
  "file_size": 104857600,
  "file_name": "Project.mov"
}
```

<h3 id="create-upload-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» folder_id|body|string|true|The ID of the folder to upload the new file to.|
|» file_size|body|integer(int64)|true|The total number of bytes of the file to be uploaded.|
|» file_name|body|string|true|The name of new file.|

|403|Forbidden|Returns an error if the operation is not allowed for some reason.<br><br>* `storage_limit_exceeded`: Account storage limit reached.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error if the parent folder could not be found, or<br>the authenticated user does not have access to it.<br><br>* `invalid_parameter`: The `folder_id` value represents a<br>  folder that the user does not have access to, or does not<br>  exist.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|Returns an error if the file already exists,<br>or the account has run out of disk space.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

## Upload part of file

<a id="opIdput_files_upload_sessions_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/upload_sessions/D5E3F7A \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'digest: sha=fpRyg5eVQletdZqEKaFlqwBXJzM=' \
  -H 'content-range: bytes 8388608-16777215/445856194' \
  --data-binary '@/path/to/file'
```

`PUT /files/upload_sessions/{upload_session_id}`

Uploads a chunk of a file for an upload session.

The actual endpoint URL is returned by the [`Create upload session`](https://developer.box.com/reference/post-files-upload-sessions)
and [`Get upload session`](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-files-upload-sessions-id) endpoints.

<h3 id="upload-part-of-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|upload_session_id|path|string|true|The ID of the upload session.|
|digest|header|string|true|The [RFC3230][1] message digest of the chunk uploaded.<br><br>`SHA-1` and `SHA-512` ([RFC5843][2]) are supported. The digest must be base64<br>encoded. The format of this header is as<br>`sha=BASE64_ENCODED_DIGEST` for `SHA-1`, or<br>`sha-512=BASE64_ENCODED_DIGEST` for `SHA-512`.<br><br>To get the value for the digest, use the<br>openSSL command to encode the file part:<br>`openssl sha1 -binary <FILE_PART_NAME> \| base64` for `SHA-1`, or<br>`openssl sha512 -binary <FILE_PART_NAME> \| base64` for `SHA-512`.<br><br>[1]: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3230<br>[2]: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5843|
|content-range|header|string|true|The byte range of the chunk.<br><br>Must not overlap with the range of a part already<br>uploaded this session. Each part’s size must be<br>exactly equal in size to the part size specified<br>in the upload session that you created.<br>One exception is the last part of the file, as this can be smaller.<br><br>When providing the value for `content-range`, remember that:<br><br>* The lower bound of each part's byte range<br>  must be a multiple of the part size.<br>* The higher bound must be a multiple of the part size - 1.|
|body|body|string(binary)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "part": {
    "part_id": "6F2D3486",
    "offset": 16777216,
    "size": 3222784,
    "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc",
    "sha512": "ae78a0ca28abffe70ac9aba830556cd6eb3fcf1501dbd9b2d7a5f45992c00812cb07b51bbd0a9174e2295671c0e86f30354afa91d281d4fbee6a323a483d6383"
  }
}
```

```json
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong"
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456"
}
```

<h3 id="upload-part-of-file-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Chunk has been uploaded successfully.<br><br>The response always includes `sha512`. It also includes<br>`sha1` if the `Digest` header used `SHA-1`.|[UploadedPart](#schemauploadedpart)|
|409|Conflict|Returns an error if the chunk conflicts with another<br>chunk previously uploaded.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|412|Precondition Failed|Returns an error if a precondition was not met.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|416|Range Not Satisfiable|Returns an error if the content range does not match a specified range<br>for the session.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Remove upload session

<a id="opIddelete_files_upload_sessions_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/upload_sessions/D5E3F7A \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /files/upload_sessions/{upload_session_id}`

Abort an upload session and discard all data uploaded.

This cannot be reversed.

The actual endpoint URL is returned by the [`Create upload session`](https://developer.box.com/reference/post-files-upload-sessions)
and [`Get upload session`](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-files-upload-sessions-id) endpoints.

<h3 id="remove-upload-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|upload_session_id|path|string|true|The ID of the upload session.|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong"
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456"
}
```

<h3 id="remove-upload-session-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|A blank response is returned if the session was<br>successfully aborted.|None|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

## Plan upload session

<a id="opIdpost_files_upload_sessions_id_plan"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/upload_sessions/D5E3F7A/plan \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "parts": [
      {
        "offset": 0,
        "size": 8388608,
        "sha512": "ae78a0ca28abffe70ac9aba830556cd6eb3fcf1501dbd9b2d7a5f45992c00812cb07b51bbd0a9174e2295671c0e86f30354afa91d281d4fbee6a323a483d6383"
      },
      {
        "offset": 8388608,
        "size": 8388608,
        "sha512": "588fde2156e1d8b23c9ca88ed3bed7bd1270e6ba0bb5b97b294ea1498952d7fd505e406097638514df92e9c5fecd0e73bd872499fcd7ea18eeb18567d0e09020"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /files/upload_sessions/{upload_session_id}/plan`

Plan an upload session by checking which parts already exist on the server.
This endpoint allows clients to optimize uploads by skipping parts that
have already been uploaded (cache hits) and only uploading missing parts.

The actual endpoint URL is returned by the [`Create upload session`](https://developer.box.com/reference/post-files-upload-sessions)
and [`Get upload session`](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-files-upload-sessions-id) endpoints.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "parts": [
    {
      "offset": 0,
      "size": 8388608,
      "sha512": "ae78a0ca28abffe70ac9aba830556cd6eb3fcf1501dbd9b2d7a5f45992c00812cb07b51bbd0a9174e2295671c0e86f30354afa91d281d4fbee6a323a483d6383"
    },
    {
      "offset": 8388608,
      "size": 8388608,
      "sha512": "588fde2156e1d8b23c9ca88ed3bed7bd1270e6ba0bb5b97b294ea1498952d7fd505e406097638514df92e9c5fecd0e73bd872499fcd7ea18eeb18567d0e09020"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="plan-upload-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|upload_session_id|path|string|true|The ID of the upload session.|
|body|body|[UploadSessionPlanRequest](#schemauploadsessionplanrequest)|false|none|
|» parts|body|[[UploadPartPlan](#schemauploadpartplan)]|true|The list of parts to check for existence.|

> Example responses

```json
      "part_id": "BFDF5379"
    }
  ],
  "misses": [

      "offset": 8388608,

    }
  ]
}
```

## Commit upload session

<a id="opIdpost_files_upload_sessions_id_commit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/upload_sessions/D5E3F7A/commit \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'digest: sha=fpRyg5eVQletdZqEKaFlqwBXJzM=' \
  -d '{
    "parts": [
      {
        "part_id": "6F2D3486",
        "offset": 16777216,
        "size": 3222784,
        "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc",
        "sha512": "ae78a0ca28abffe70ac9aba830556cd6eb3fcf1501dbd9b2d7a5f45992c00812cb07b51bbd0a9174e2295671c0e86f30354afa91d281d4fbee6a323a483d6383"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /files/upload_sessions/{upload_session_id}/commit`

Close an upload session and create a file from the uploaded chunks.

The actual endpoint URL is returned by the [`Create upload session`](https://developer.box.com/reference/post-files-upload-sessions)
and [`Get upload session`](https://developer.box.com/reference/get-files-upload-sessions-id) endpoints.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "parts": [
    {
      "part_id": "6F2D3486",
      "offset": 16777216,
      "size": 3222784,
      "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc",
      "sha512": "ae78a0ca28abffe70ac9aba830556cd6eb3fcf1501dbd9b2d7a5f45992c00812cb07b51bbd0a9174e2295671c0e86f30354afa91d281d4fbee6a323a483d6383"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="commit-upload-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|upload_session_id|path|string|true|The ID of the upload session.|
|digest|header|string|true|The [RFC3230][1] message digest of the whole file.<br><br>Only SHA1 is supported. The SHA1 digest must be Base64<br>encoded. The format of this header is as<br>`sha=BASE64_ENCODED_DIGEST`.<br><br>`SHA-512` is not supported for the whole-file digest, even if<br>the parts were uploaded with `SHA-512` digests.<br><br>[1]: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3230|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|
|if-none-match|header|string|false|Ensures an item is only returned if it has changed.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `304 Not Modified` if the item has not<br>changed since.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» parts|body|[[UploadPart](#schemauploadpart)]|true|The list details for the uploaded parts.<br><br>Each entry can include `sha1` or `sha512`. Include `sha512`<br>on every entry or on none of them. A request where only<br>some entries include `sha512` is rejected.<br><br>Include parts that the server already has, returned as<br>`hits` by the [`Plan upload session`](https://developer.box.com/reference/post-files-upload-sessions-id-plan)<br>endpoint. Use the `part_id`, `offset`, and `size` from the<br>plan response. If the other entries include `sha512`,<br>include the `sha512` value from the plan response.<br>Otherwise, leave the hash out of these entries.|

<h3 id="commit-upload-session-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returns the file object in a list.|[Files](#schemafiles)|
|202|Accepted|Returns when all chunks have been uploaded but not yet processed.<br><br>Inspect the upload session to get more information about the<br>progress of processing the chunks, then retry committing the file<br>when all chunks have processed.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if the request body is not valid.<br><br>* `invalid_parts_field` - Only some entries in `parts` include<br>  `sha512`. Include `sha512` on every entry or on none of them.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|Returns an error if there is already a file with the same name<br>in the target folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|412|Precondition Failed|Returns an error if the `If-Match` or `If-None-Match` conditions fail.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Retry-After|integer||Indicates the number of seconds the client should wait before<br>attempting their commit request again.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

<h1 id="box-platform-api-user-avatars">User avatars</h1>

User avatars are JPG or PNG files
uploaded to Box to represent the
user image. They are then displayed
in the user account.

## Get user avatar

<a id="opIdget_users_id_avatar"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/users/12345/avatar \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users/{user_id}/avatar`

Retrieves an image of a the user's avatar.

<h3 id="get-user-avatar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user.|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong"
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456"
}
```

<h3 id="get-user-avatar-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|When an avatar can be found for the user the<br>image data will be returned in the body of the<br>response.|Inline|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Add or update user avatar

<a id="opIdpost_users_id_avatar"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/users/12345/avatar \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'pic=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /users/{user_id}/avatar`

Adds or updates a user avatar.

> Body parameter

```yaml
pic: string
```

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» pic|body|string(binary)|true|The image file to be uploaded to Box.<br>Accepted file extensions are `.jpg` or `.png`.<br>The maximum file size is 1MB.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-users">Users</h1>

Box API supports a variety of users,
ranging from real employees
logging in with their Managed User account,
to applications using App Users to drive powerful
automation workflows.

## List enterprise users

<a id="opIdget_users"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users`

Returns a list of all users for the Enterprise along with their `user_id`,
`public_name`, and `login`.

The application and the authenticated user need to
have the permission to look up users in the entire
enterprise.

<h3 id="list-enterprise-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter_term|query|string|false|Limits the results to only users who's `name` or<br>`login` start with the search term.<br><br>For externally managed users, the search term needs<br>to completely match the in order to find the user, and<br>it will only return one user at a time.|
|user_type|query|string|false|Limits the results to the kind of user specified.<br><br>* `all` returns every kind of user for whom the<br>  `login` or `name` partially matches the<br>  `filter_term`. It will only return an external user<br>  if the login matches the `filter_term` completely,<br>  and in that case it will only return that user.<br>* `managed` returns all managed and app users for whom<br>  the `login` or `name` partially matches the<br>  `filter_term`.<br>* `external` returns all external users for whom the<br>  `login` matches the `filter_term` exactly.|
|external_app_user_id|query|string|false|Limits the results to app users with the given<br>`external_app_user_id` value.<br><br>When creating an app user, an<br>`external_app_user_id` value can be set. This value can<br>then be used in this endpoint to find any users that<br>match that `external_app_user_id` value.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|usemarker|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether to use marker-based pagination instead of<br>offset-based pagination. Only one pagination method can<br>be used at a time.<br><br>By setting this value to true, the API will return a `marker` field<br>that can be passed as a parameter to this endpoint to get the next<br>page of the response.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|user_type|all|
|user_type|managed|
|user_type|external|

## Create user

<a id="opIdpost_users"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Aaron Levie",
    "login": "boss@box.com",
    "is_platform_access_only": true,
    "role": "user",
    "language": "en",
    "is_sync_enabled": true,
    "job_title": "CEO",
    "phone": "6509241374",
    "address": "900 Jefferson Ave, Redwood City, CA 94063",
    "space_amount": 11345156112,
    "tracking_codes": [
      {
        "type": "tracking_code",
        "name": "department",
        "value": "Sales"
      }
    ],
    "can_see_managed_users": true,
    "timezone": "Africa/Bujumbura",
    "is_external_collab_restricted": true,
    "is_exempt_from_device_limits": true,
    "is_exempt_from_login_verification": true,
    "status": "active",
    "external_app_user_id": "my-user-1234"
  }'
```

`POST /users`

Creates a new managed user in an enterprise. This endpoint
is only available to users and applications with the right
admin permissions.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Aaron Levie",
  "login": "boss@box.com",
  "is_platform_access_only": true,
  "role": "user",
  "language": "en",
  "is_sync_enabled": true,
  "job_title": "CEO",
  "phone": "6509241374",
  "address": "900 Jefferson Ave, Redwood City, CA 94063",
  "space_amount": 11345156112,
  "tracking_codes": [
    {
      "type": "tracking_code",
      "name": "department",
      "value": "Sales"
    }
  ],
  "can_see_managed_users": true,
  "timezone": "Africa/Bujumbura",
  "is_external_collab_restricted": true,
  "is_exempt_from_device_limits": true,
  "is_exempt_from_login_verification": true,
  "status": "active",
  "external_app_user_id": "my-user-1234"
}
```

<h3 id="create-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the user.|
|» login|body|string|false|The email address the user uses to log in<br><br>Required, unless `is_platform_access_only`<br>is set to `true`.|
|» is_platform_access_only|body|boolean|false|Specifies that the user is an app user.|
|» role|body|string|false|The user’s enterprise role.|
|» language|body|string|false|The language of the user, formatted in modified version of the<br>[ISO 639-1](https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/language-codes) format.|
|» is_sync_enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the user can use Box Sync.|
|» job_title|body|string|false|The user’s job title.|
|» phone|body|string|false|The user’s phone number.|
|» address|body|string|false|The user’s address.|
|» space_amount|body|integer(int64)|false|The user’s total available space in bytes. Set this to `-1` to<br>indicate unlimited storage.|
|» tracking_codes|body|[[TrackingCode](#schematrackingcode)]|false|Tracking codes allow an admin to generate reports from the<br>admin console and assign an attribute to a specific group<br>of users. This setting must be enabled for an enterprise before it<br>can be used.|
|» can_see_managed_users|body|boolean|false|Whether the user can see other enterprise users in their<br>contact list.|
|» timezone|body|string(timezone)|false|The user's timezone.|
|» is_external_collab_restricted|body|boolean|false|Whether the user is allowed to collaborate with users outside<br>their enterprise.|
|» is_exempt_from_device_limits|body|boolean|false|Whether to exempt the user from enterprise device limits.|
|» is_exempt_from_login_verification|body|boolean|false|Whether the user must use two-factor authentication.|
|» status|body|string|false|The user's account status.|
|» external_app_user_id|body|string|false|An external identifier for an app user, which can be used to look<br>up the user. This can be used to tie user IDs from external<br>identity providers to Box users.|

## Get current user

<a id="opIdget_users_me"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/users/me \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users/me`

Retrieves information about the user who is currently authenticated.

In the case of a client-side authenticated OAuth 2.0 application
this will be the user who authorized the app.

In the case of a JWT, server-side authenticated application
this will be the service account that belongs to the application
by default.

Use the `As-User` header to change who this API call is made on behalf of.

`PUT /users/{user_id}`

Updates a managed or app user in an enterprise. This endpoint
is only available to users and applications with the right
admin permissions.

> Body parameter


<h3 id="update-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» enterprise|body|string \| null|false|Set this to `null` to roll the user out of the enterprise<br>and make them a free user.|
|» notify|body|boolean|false|Whether the user should receive an email when they<br>are rolled out of an enterprise.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the user.|
|» login|body|string|false|The email address the user uses to log in<br><br>Note: If the target user's email is not confirmed, then the<br>primary login address cannot be changed.|
|» role|body|string|false|The user’s enterprise role.|
|» language|body|string|false|The language of the user, formatted in modified version of the<br>[ISO 639-1](https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/language-codes) format.|
|» is_sync_enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the user can use Box Sync.|
|» job_title|body|string|false|The user’s job title.|
|» phone|body|string|false|The user’s phone number.|
|» address|body|string|false|The user’s address.|
|» tracking_codes|body|[[TrackingCode](#schematrackingcode)]|false|Tracking codes allow an admin to generate reports from the<br>admin console and assign an attribute to a specific group<br>of users. This setting must be enabled for an enterprise before it<br>can be used.|
|» can_see_managed_users|body|boolean|false|Whether the user can see other enterprise users in their<br>contact list.|
|» timezone|body|string(timezone)|false|The user's timezone.|
|» is_external_collab_restricted|body|boolean|false|Whether the user is allowed to collaborate with users outside<br>their enterprise.|
|» is_exempt_from_device_limits|body|boolean|false|Whether to exempt the user from enterprise device limits.|
|» is_exempt_from_login_verification|body|boolean|false|Whether the user must use two-factor authentication.|
|» is_password_reset_required|body|boolean|false|Whether the user is required to reset their password.|
|» is_collaborated_content_available_when_owner_inactive|body|boolean|false|Whether collaborators can access content owned by the user when<br>the user is inactive. This setting preserves existing<br>collaborator access and does not grant new permissions.|
|» status|body|string|false|The user's account status.|
|» space_amount|body|integer(int64)|false|The user’s total available space in bytes. Set this to `-1` to<br>indicate unlimited storage.|
|» notification_email|body|object \| null|false|An alternate notification email address to which email<br>notifications are sent. When it's confirmed, this will be<br>the email address to which notifications are sent instead of<br>to the primary email address.<br><br>Set this value to `null` to remove the notification email.|
|» » email|body|string|false|The email address to send the notifications to.|
|» external_app_user_id|body|string|false|An external identifier for an app user, which can be used to look<br>up the user. This can be used to tie user IDs from external<br>identity providers to Box users.<br><br>Note: In order to update this field, you need to request a token<br>using the application that created the app user.|

|» status|inactive|
|» status|cannot_delete_edit|
|» status|cannot_delete_edit_upload|

## Delete user

<a id="opIddelete_users_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/users/12345 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /users/{user_id}`

Deletes a user. By default, this operation fails if the user
still owns any content. 
To proceed, move their owned content first, or use the `force` parameter to delete
the user and their files.

If the enterprise has a retention policy, including a retired one, or a
legal hold that is not fully released, you can't delete a user who owns
content, even with `force`. Transfer the user's content first by using the
[Transfer owned folders](https://developer.box.com/reference/put-users-id-folders-0)
endpoint.

<h3 id="delete-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user.|
|notify|query|boolean|false|Whether the user will receive email notification of<br>the deletion.|
|force|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether to delete the user even if they still own files.<br><br>If the user owns content and the enterprise has a retention policy,<br>including a retired one, or a legal hold that is not fully released,<br>setting `force` to `true` doesn't delete the user. The request returns<br>a `403` error, and you must transfer the user's content before deleting<br>the user.|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong"
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong"
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Removes the user and returns an empty response.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returns an error if the user can't be deleted.<br><br>* `forbidden` with the message<br>  `User cannot be deleted due to retention policies. Please transfer user content first`<br>  when the user owns content and the enterprise has a retention policy,<br>  including a retired one, or a legal hold that is not fully released. This applies<br>  even if none of the policies apply to the user's content, and even<br>  when `force` is set to `true`. Transfer the user's content by using the<br>  [Transfer owned folders](https://developer.box.com/reference/put-users-id-folders-0)<br>  endpoint, then try again.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

<h1 id="box-platform-api-watermarks-files">Watermarks (Files)</h1>

A watermark is a semi-transparent
overlay on an embedded file
preview that displays a viewer's email address
or user ID and the time of access over
the file.

## Get watermark on file

<a id="opIdget_files_id_watermark"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/files/12345/watermark \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /files/{file_id}/watermark`

Retrieve the watermark for a file.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-watermarks-folders">Watermarks (Folders)</h1>

A watermark is a semi-transparent overlay on an embedded folder
preview that displays a viewer's email address or user ID
and the time of access over
the folder content.

## Get watermark for folder

<a id="opIdget_folders_id_watermark"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /folders/{folder_id}/watermark`

|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-web-links">Web links</h1>

Web links are objects that point to URLs.
These objects are also known as bookmarks
within the Box web application.

## Create web link

<a id="opIdpost_web_links"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/web_links \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://box.com",
    "parent": {
      "id": "0"
    },
    "name": "Box Website",
    "description": "Cloud Content Management"
  }'
```

`POST /web_links`

Creates a web link object within a folder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "url": "https://box.com",
  "parent": {
    "id": "0"
  },
  "name": "Box Website",
  "description": "Cloud Content Management"
}
```

<h3 id="create-web-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» url|body|string|true|The URL that this web link links to. Must start with<br>`"http://"` or `"https://"`.|
|» parent|body|object|true|The parent folder to create the web link within.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of parent folder.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the web link. Defaults to the URL if not set.|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the web link.|

```json
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link",
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "one_time_passcode": {
      "mode": "none"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-web-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|web_link_id|path|string|true|The ID of the web link.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» url|body|string|false|The new URL that the web link links to. Must start with<br>`"http://"` or `"https://"`.|
|» parent|body|object|false|none|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of parent item.|
|» » user_id|body|string|false|The input for `user_id` is optional. Moving to non-root folder is not allowed when `user_id` is present. Parent folder id should be zero when `user_id` is provided.|
|» name|body|string|false|A new name for the web link. Defaults to the URL if not set.|
|» description|body|string|false|A new description of the web link.|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|The settings for the shared link to update.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string \| null|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br>Passwords must now be at least eight characters<br>long and include a number, upper case letter, or<br>a non-numeric or non-alphabetic character.<br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared<br>links.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts. The value must be greater than the<br>current date and time.|
|» » one_time_passcode|body|object|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableNone](#schemasharedlinkotpwritablenone)|false|One-time-passcode (OTP) enforcement is turned off. The shared link is<br>accessible without any one-time-passcode verification.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableOpen](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableopen)|false|Any anonymous recipient can request a one-time-passcode to any email<br>address and access the shared link after verifying it. Collaborators<br>and registered Box users access the link without being prompted.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[SharedLinkOtpWritableAllowlist](#schemasharedlinkotpwritableallowlist)|false|Anonymous recipients can request a one-time-passcode only when they<br>enter an email that matches an entry on the `allowlist`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-webhooks">Webhooks</h1>

Webhooks allow you to monitor Box content for events,
and receive notifications to a URL of your choice when they occur.
For example, a workflow may include waiting
for a file to be downloaded to delete a shared link.

## List all webhooks

<a id="opIdget_webhooks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/webhooks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /webhooks`

Returns all defined webhooks for the requesting application.

This API only returns webhooks that are applied to files or folders that are
owned by the authenticated user. This means that an admin can not see webhooks
created by a service account unless the admin has access to those folders, and
vice versa.

<h3 id="list-all-webhooks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

## Create webhook

<a id="opIdpost_webhooks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/webhooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "target": {
      "id": "1231232",
      "type": "file"
    },
    "address": "https://example.com/webhooks",
    "triggers": [
      "FILE.UPLOADED"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /webhooks`

Creates a webhook.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "target": {
    "id": "1231232",

}
```

<h1 id="box-platform-api-workflows">Workflows</h1>

Box Relay Workflows are objects that represent
a named collection of flows.

## List workflows

<a id="opIdget_workflows"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.box.com/2.0/workflows?folder_id=12345' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /workflows`

Returns list of workflows that act on a given `folder ID`, and
have a flow with a trigger type of `WORKFLOW_MANUAL_START`.

You application must be authorized to use the `Manage Box Relay` application
scope within the developer console in to use this endpoint.

<h3 id="list-workflows-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|query|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|trigger_type|query|string|false|Type of trigger to search for.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-zip-downloads">Zip Downloads</h1>

Zip downloads represent a successful request
to create a ZIP archive with files and folders.

## Create zip download

<a id="opIdpost_zip_downloads"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/zip_downloads \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "items": [
      {
        "type": "file",
        "id": "12345"
      }
    ],
    "download_file_name": "January Financials"
  }'
```

`POST /zip_downloads`

Creates a request to download multiple files and folders as a single `zip`
archive file. This API does not return the archive but instead performs all
the checks to ensure that the user has access to all the items, and then
returns a `download_url` and a `status_url` that can be used to download the
archive.

The limit for an archive is either the Account's upload limit or
10,000 files, whichever is met first.

**Note**: Downloading a large file can be
affected by various
factors such as distance, network latency,
bandwidth, and congestion, as well as packet loss
ratio and current server load.
For these reasons we recommend that a maximum ZIP archive
total size does not exceed 25GB.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "type": "file",
      "id": "12345"
    }
  ],
  "download_file_name": "January Financials"
}
```

<h3 id="create-zip-download-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ZipDownloadRequest](#schemazipdownloadrequest)|false|none|
|» items|body|[object]|true|A list of items to add to the `zip` archive. These can<br>be folders or files.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of the item to add to the archive.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The identifier of the item to add to the archive. When this item is<br>a folder then this can not be the root folder with ID `0`.|
|» download_file_name|body|string|false|The optional name of the `zip` archive. This name will be appended by the<br>`.zip` file extension, for example `January Financials.zip`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|file|
|» » type|folder|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "download_url": "https://dl.boxcloud.com/2.0/zip_downloads/29l00nfxDyHOt7RphI9zT_w==nDnZEDjY2S8iEWWCHEEiptFxwoWojjlibZjJ6geuE5xnXENDTPxzgbks_yY=/content",
  "status_url": "https://api.box.com/2.0/zip_downloads/29l00nfxDyHOt7RphI9zT_w==nDnZEDjY2S8iEWWCHEEiptFxwoWojjlibZjJ6geuE5xnXENDTPxzgbks_yY=/status",
  "expires_at": "2020-07-22T11:26:08Z",
  "name_conflicts": [
    [
      {
        "id": "12345",
        "type": "file",
        "original_name": "Report.pdf",
        "download_name": "3aa6a7.pdf"
      },
      {
        "id": "34325",
        "type": "file",
        "original_name": "Report.pdf",
        "download_name": "5d53f2.pdf"
      }
    ]
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-zip-download-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|If the `zip` archive is ready to be downloaded, the API will return a<br>response that will include a `download_url`, a `status_url`, as well as<br>any conflicts that might have occurred when creating the request.|[ZipDownload](#schemazipdownload)|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if some of the parameters are missing or<br>not valid.<br><br>In most cases, this error might happen because the JSON request body is<br>not valid JSON, any of the items has an incorrect or missing ID, any of<br>the items is not a file or folder, or the root folder with ID `0` has been<br>added to the list of folders to add to the archive.<br><br>The following is a list of common error codes for this response.<br><br>* `bad_request` - the request body is missing, invalid, or both the list<br>of files and folders are empty. Additionally, it this error might be<br>returned when attempting to add the root folder with ID `0` to an archive.<br>* `zip_download_file_count_exceeded_limit` - the requested files and<br>folders would result in an archive with more than 10,000 files. The<br>request will have to be split into multiple requests to reduce the number<br>of files per archive.<br>* `zip_download_pre_compressed_bytes_exceeded_limit` - the requested files<br>and folders would result in an archive with more than the allowed download<br>limit. The request will have to be split into multiple requests to reduce<br>the size of the archive.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned when the access token provided in the `Authorization` header<br>is not recognized or not provided.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned when an authorization header is provided but the user does not<br>have access to the items.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Download zip archive

<a id="opIdget_zip_downloads_id_content"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/zip_downloads/Lu6fA9Ob-jyysp3AAvMF4AkLEwZwAYbL%3Dtgj2zIC%3DeK9RvJnJbjJl9rNh2qBgHDpyOCAOhpM%3Dvajg2mKq8Mdd/content \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /zip_downloads/{zip_download_id}/content`

Returns the contents of a `zip` archive in binary format. This URL does not
require any form of authentication and could be used in a user's browser to
download the archive to a user's device.

By default, this URL is only valid for a few seconds from the creation of
the request for this archive. Once a download has started it can not be
stopped and resumed, instead a new request for a zip archive would need to
be created.

The URL of this endpoint should not be considered as fixed. Instead, use
the [Create zip download](https://developer.box.com/reference/post-zip-downloads) API to request to create a
`zip` archive, and then follow the `download_url` field in the response to
this endpoint.

<h3 id="download-zip-archive-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zip_download_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent this `zip` archive.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong"
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong"
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong"
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456"
}
```

<h3 id="download-zip-archive-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the content of the items requested for this download, formatted as<br>a stream of files and folders in a `zip` archive.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error if the ID of this download request is not valid. This<br>error can also be returned if this URL has been called before. To<br>re-download this archive, please create a new request for a zip download.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Returns an error if the number of concurrent zip downloads has been<br>reached for either the user or the enterprise.<br><br>* `user_too_many_concurrent_downloads` - the maximum of 5 parallel<br>downloads of zip archives per user has been met.<br>* `enterprise_too_many_concurrent_downloads` - the maximum of 10 parallel<br>downloads of zip archives per enterprise has been met.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Content-Disposition|string||The name of the archive to be downloaded.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get zip download status

<a id="opIdget_zip_downloads_id_status"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.box.com/2.0/zip_downloads/Lu6fA9Ob-jyysp3AAvMF4AkLEwZwAYbL%3Dtgj2zIC%3DeK9RvJnJbjJl9rNh2qBgHDpyOCAOhpM%3Dvajg2mKq8Mdd/status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zip_downloads/{zip_download_id}/status`

Returns the download status of a `zip` archive, allowing an application to
inspect the progress of the download as well as the number of items that
might have been skipped.

This endpoint can only be accessed once the download has started.
Subsequently this endpoint is valid for 12 hours from the start of the
download.

The URL of this endpoint should not be considered as fixed. Instead, use
the [Create zip download](https://developer.box.com/reference/post-zip-downloads) API to request to create a
`zip` archive, and then follow the `status_url` field in the response to
this endpoint.

<h3 id="get-zip-download-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|zip_download_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent this `zip` archive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "total_file_count": 20,
  "downloaded_file_count": 10,
  "skipped_file_count": 5,
  "skipped_folder_count": 5,
  "state": "succeeded"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong"
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456"
}
```

<h3 id="get-zip-download-status-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the status of the `zip` archive that is being downloaded.|[ZipDownloadStatus](#schemazipdownloadstatus)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned when the access token provided in the `Authorization` header<br>is not recognized or not provided.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned when an authorization header is provided but the user does not<br>have access to the items.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error if the ID of this download request is not valid, or if<br>the status of a download is requested before the download has been<br>started.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

A token that can be used to make authenticated API calls.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_token|string(token)|false|none|The requested access token.|
|expires_in|integer(int64)|false|none|The time in seconds by which this token will expire.|
|token_type|string|false|none|The type of access token returned.|
|restricted_to|[[ResourceScope](#schemaresourcescope)]|false|none|The permissions that this access token permits,<br>providing a list of resources (files, folders, etc)<br>and the scopes permitted for each of those resources.|
|refresh_token|string(token)|false|none|The refresh token for this access token, which can be used<br>to request a new access token when the current one expires.|
|issued_token_type|string(urn)|false|none|The type of downscoped access token returned. This is only<br>returned if an access token has been downscoped.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|token_type|bearer|
|issued_token_type|urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token|

AI ask request object.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mode|string|true|none|Box AI handles text documents with text representations up to 2MB in size, or a maximum of 25 files,<br>whichever comes first. If the text file size exceeds 2MB, the first 2MB of text representation will be processed.<br>Box AI handles image documents with a resolution of 1024 x 1024 pixels, with a maximum of 5 images or 5 pages<br>for multi-page images. If the number of image or image pages exceeds 5, the first 5 images or pages will<br>be processed. If you set mode parameter to `single_item_qa`, the items array can have one element only.<br>Currently Box AI does not support multi-modal requests. If both images and text are sent Box AI will only<br>process the text.|
|prompt|string|true|none|The prompt provided by the client to be answered by the LLM.<br>The prompt's length is limited to 10000 characters.|
|items|[[AiItemAsk](#schemaaiitemask)]|true|none|The items to be processed by the LLM, often files.<br>To search across and ask questions about the contents of a Box Hub,<br>pass a single item with `type` set to `hubs`. See the item `type`<br>property for details.|
|dialogue_history|[[AiDialogueHistory](#schemaaidialoguehistory)]|false|none|The history of prompts and answers previously passed to the LLM. This provides additional context to the LLM in generating the response.|
|include_citations|boolean|false|none|A flag to indicate whether citations should be returned.|
|ai_agent|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_AiExtractStructured">AiExtractStructured</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaiextractstructured"></a>
<a id="schema_AiExtractStructured"></a>
<a id="tocSaiextractstructured"></a>
<a id="tocsaiextractstructured"></a>

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "123",
      "type": "file",
      "content": "This is file content."
    }
  ],
  "metadata_template": {
    "template_key": "invoiceTemplate",
    "type": "metadata_template",
    "scope": "enterprise_12345"
  },
  "fields": [
    {
      "key": "name",
      "description": "The name of the person.",
      "displayName": "Name",
      "prompt": "Name is the first and last name from the email address",
      "type": "enum",
      "options": [
        {
          "key": "First Name"
        },
        {
          "key": "Last Name"
        }
      ],
      "fields": [
        {
          "key": "street_name",
          "description": "The street name of the address.",
          "displayName": "Street Name",
          "prompt": "The street name from the address section",
          "type": "string",
          "options": [
            {
              "key": "First Name"
            }
          ]
        }
      ],
      "taxonomy_key": "certification_taxonomy",
      "namespace": "enterprise_123",
      "options_rules": {
        "multiSelect": false,
        "selectableLevels": [
          1,
          2
        ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "ai_agent": {
    "type": "ai_agent_id",
    "id": "14031"
  },
  "include_confidence_score": true,
  "include_reference": true,
  "taxonomy_sources": [
    {
      "type": "taxonomy",
      "taxonomy_key": "certification_taxonomy",
      "namespace": "enterprise_123"
    },
    {
      "type": "file",
      "taxonomy_key": "industry_taxonomy",
      "id": "1234567890"
    }
  ]
}
```

AI Extract Structured Request object.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|items|[[AiItem--Base](#schemaaiitem--base)]|true|none|The items to be processed by the LLM. Currently you can use files only.|
|metadata_template|object|false|none|The metadata template containing the fields to extract.<br>For your request to work, you must provide either `metadata_template` or `fields`, but not both.|
|fields|[object]|false|none|The fields to be extracted from the provided items.<br>For your request to work, you must provide either `metadata_template` or `fields`, but not both.|
|ai_agent|object|false|none|none|
|include_confidence_score|boolean|false|none|A flag to indicate whether confidence scores for every extracted field should be returned. Estimates the likelihood that an extracted metadata field value is accurate and correct. Displays a numerical and categorical confidence score to help users and automated systems quickly determine extraction reliability.|
|include_reference|boolean|false|none|A flag to indicate whether references for every extracted field should be returned. References and bounding boxes show where the agent extracted the metadata from. They help you check for accuracy and fix any mistakes. References are short, exact quotes from the original document used to verify results. Bounding boxes highlight the specific areas on the page where that text is found.|
|taxonomy_sources|[[AiTaxonomySource](#schemaaitaxonomysource)]|false|none|The taxonomy sources to be used for the structured extraction. They can either be an existing file or a taxonomy.<br>For your request to work, `fields` must also be provided. `taxonomy_sources` is not supported with `metadata_template`.|

So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability <br>mass are considered. We generally recommend altering this or temperature but not both.|

<h2 id="tocS_AiLlmEndpointParamsGoogle">AiLlmEndpointParamsGoogle</h2>


AI LLM endpoint params Google object.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the AI LLM endpoint params object for Google.<br>This parameter is **required**.|
|temperature|number \| null|false|none|The temperature is used for sampling during response generation, which occurs when `top-P` and `top-K` are applied. Temperature controls the degree of randomness in the token selection.|
|top_p|number \| null|false|none|`Top-P` changes how the model selects tokens for output. Tokens are selected from the most (see `top-K`) to least probable until the sum of their probabilities equals the `top-P` value.|
|top_k|number \| null|false|none|`Top-K` changes how the model selects tokens for output. A low `top-K` means the next selected token is<br>the most probable among all tokens in the model's vocabulary (also called greedy decoding),<br>while a high `top-K` means that the next token is selected from among the three most probable tokens by using temperature.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|google_params|

```json
{
  "type": "openai_params",
  "temperature": 0,
  "top_p": 1,

  "stop": "<|im_end|>"
}
```

AI LLM endpoint params OpenAI object.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the AI LLM endpoint params object for OpenAI.<br>This parameter is **required**.|
|temperature|number \| null|false|none|What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, <br>while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. <br>We generally recommend altering this or `top_p` but not both.|
|top_p|number \| null|false|none|An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results <br>of the tokens with `top_p` probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability <br>mass are considered. We generally recommend altering this or temperature but not both.|
|frequency_penalty|number \| null|false|none|A number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on their existing frequency in the <br>text so far, decreasing the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim.|
|presence_penalty|number \| null|false|none|A number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to talk about new topics.|
|stop|string \| null|false|none|Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|openai_params|

An object for a `taxonomy` type template field containing configuration for taxonomy options. Required if using `taxonomy` type field.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of the AI Agent.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of agent used to handle queries.|
|origin|string|true|none|The provider of the AI Agent.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the AI Agent.|
|access_state|string|true|none|The state of the AI Agent. Possible values are: `enabled`, `disabled`, and `enabled_for_selected_users`.|
|created_by|object|false|none|The user who created this agent.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|The ISO date-time formatted timestamp of when this AI agent was created.|
|modified_by|object|false|none|The user who most recently modified this agent.|
|modified_at|string(date-time)|false|none|The ISO date-time formatted timestamp of when this AI agent was recently modified.|
|icon_reference|string|false|none|The icon reference of the AI Agent.|
|allowed_entities|[[AiAgentAllowedEntity](#schemaaiagentallowedentity)]|false|none|List of allowed users or groups.|

|---|---|

Collaborations define access permissions for users and groups to files and
folders, similar to access control lists. A collaboration object grants a
user or group access to a file or folder with permissions defined by a
specific role.

### Properties

|type|string|true|none|The value will always be `collaboration`.|

|app_item|object \| null|false|none|none|
|accessible_by|[CollaborationAccessGrantee](#schemacollaborationaccessgrantee)|false|none|The user or group that is granted access.|
|invite_email|string \| null|false|none|The email address used to invite an unregistered collaborator, if<br>they are not a registered user.|
|role|string|false|none|The level of access granted.|
|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the collaboration will expire, or `null` if no expiration<br>date is set.|
|is_access_only|boolean|false|none|If set to `true`, collaborators have access to<br>shared items, but such items won't be visible in the<br>All Files list. Additionally, collaborators won't<br>see the path to the root folder for the<br>shared item.|
|status|string|false|none|The status of the collaboration invitation. If the status<br>is `pending`, `name` returns an empty string.|
|acknowledged_at|string(date-time)|false|none|When the `status` of the collaboration object changed to<br>`accepted` or `rejected`.|
|created_by|object|false|none|none|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|When the collaboration object was created.|
|modified_at|string(date-time)|false|none|When the collaboration object was last modified.|
|acceptance_requirements_status|object|false|none|none|

|content_created_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The date and time at which this file was originally<br>created, which might be before it was uploaded to Box.|
|content_modified_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The date and time at which this file was last updated,<br>which might be before it was uploaded to Box.|
|created_by|object|false|none|none|
|modified_by|object|false|none|none|
|owned_by|object|false|none|none|
|shared_link|object \| null|false|none|none|
|parent|object \| null|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|etag|string \| null|false|none|The HTTP `etag` of this file. This can be used within some API<br>endpoints in the `If-Match` and `If-None-Match` headers to only<br>perform changes on the file if (no) changes have happened.|

|file_version|object|false|none|none|

|created_by|object|false|none|none|
|modified_by|object|false|none|none|
|owned_by|object|false|none|none|
|shared_link|object \| null|false|none|none|
|parent|object \| null|false|none|none|
|item_status|string|false|none|Defines if this item has been deleted or not.<br><br>* `active` when the item has is not in the trash<br>* `trashed` when the item has been moved to the trash but not deleted<br>* `deleted` when the item has been permanently deleted.|
|version_number|string|false|none|The version number of this file.|
|comment_count|integer|false|none|The number of comments on this file.|
|permissions|object|false|none|none|
|tags|object|false|none|none|
|lock|object \| null|false|none|none|
|extension|string|false|none|Indicates the (optional) file extension for this file. By default,<br>this is set to an empty string.|
|is_package|boolean|false|none|Indicates if the file is a package. Packages are commonly used<br>by Mac Applications and can include iWork files.|
|expiring_embed_link|object|false|none|none|
|watermark_info|object|false|none|none|
|is_accessible_via_shared_link|boolean|false|none|Specifies if the file can be accessed<br>via the direct shared link or a shared link<br>to a parent folder.|
|allowed_invitee_roles|[string]|false|none|A list of the types of roles that user can be invited at<br>when sharing this file.|
|is_externally_owned|boolean|false|none|Specifies if this file is owned by a user outside of the<br>authenticated enterprise.|
|has_collaborations|boolean|false|none|Specifies if this file has any other collaborators.|
|metadata|object|false|none|none|
|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the file will automatically be deleted.|
|representations|object|false|none|none|
|classification|object \| null|false|none|none|
|uploader_display_name|object|false|none|none|
|disposition_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The retention expiration timestamp for the given file.|
|shared_link_permission_options|[string]|false|none|A list of the types of roles that user can be invited at<br>when sharing this file.|
|is_associated_with_app_item|boolean|false|none|This field will return true if the file or any ancestor of the file<br>is associated with at least one app item. Note that this will return<br>true even if the context user does not have access to the app item(s)<br>associated with the file.|
|collections|[[Collection](#schemacollection)]|false|none|The collections that this file belongs to.<br><br>For more information, see the<br>[collections guide](https://developer.box.com/guides/collections).|
|is_download_available|boolean|false|none|Whether the file's binary content is eligible to be downloaded.<br><br>This is a content-level flag and does not reflect whether the<br>current user is authorized to download the file. Use<br>`permissions.can_download`, when available, for that.|

Unlike `download_url`, authorization is<br>evaluated when the URL is requested with a valid access token.<br><br>This field is only returned for files, not folders or web links.|

This defaults<br>to `active`.<br><br>When the status is set to `inactive`, the file request<br>will no longer accept new submissions, and any visitor<br>to the file request URL will receive a `HTTP 404` status<br>code.<br><br>This defaults to status of file request that was<br>copied to create this file request.|

|expires_at|string(date-time)|false|none|The date after which a file request will no longer accept new<br>submissions.<br><br>After this date, the `status` will automatically be set to<br>`inactive`.|
|folder|object|true|none|none|
|url|string|false|read-only|The generated URL for this file request. This URL can be shared<br>with users to let them upload files to the associated folder.|

By providing that<br>header, a change will only be performed on the  file request if the `etag`<br>on the file request still matches the `etag` provided in the `If-Match`<br>header.|
|created_by|object|false|none|none|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|The date and time when the file request was created.|
|updated_by|object|false|none|none|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|The date and time when the file request was last updated.|
